questions.stem: A previously healthy 3-year-old girl is brought to the emergency department with fever and neck stiffness. Cerebrospinal fluid culture grows an organism whose outermost layer is a polysaccharide coat lying external to the cell wall. This structure most directly contributes to virulence by which of the following mechanisms?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Anchoring the organism to mucosal epithelial cells

choices.label: B
choices.text: Hydrolyzing beta-lactam drugs in the periplasmic space

choices.label: C
choices.text: Permitting transport of small molecules across the membrane

choices.label: D
choices.text: Protecting the organism from host phagocytosis

choices.label: E
choices.text: Triggering cytokine release through toll-like receptors

explanation.summary: The bacterial capsule is a polysaccharide layer whose primary function is protection from host immune defenses such as phagocytosis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Capsules are present in some gram-positive and some gram-negative bacteria and are typically composed of polysaccharides. Their primary function is to shield the bacterium from host immune defenses, notably phagocytosis. By promoting survival within the host, a capsule often enhances an organism's ability to cause disease.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Adhesion to host surfaces is the job of pili and fimbriae, which carry adhesin proteins and glycoproteins; the capsule is not described as the adhesion structure.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Beta-lactamase activity is localized to the periplasmic space of gram-negative organisms, a compartment between the outer and inner membranes, not to the capsule.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Transport of molecules across the outer membrane is performed by porins, protein channels of gram-negative bacteria.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Systemic immune activation through toll-like receptors is the property of lipopolysaccharide in the gram-negative outer membrane, not of the polysaccharide capsule.

questions.stem: A 69-year-old man is brought to the emergency department with a temperature of 39.4 C, blood pressure of 78/40 mm Hg, mental confusion, and large patches of bruising over his torso. Blood cultures grow a gram-negative organism. Which of the following bacterial components is most directly responsible for his presentation?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Dormant spores within the organism

choices.label: B
choices.text: Lipopolysaccharide of the outer membrane

choices.label: C
choices.text: Lipoteichoic acid of the cell wall

choices.label: D
choices.text: Mycolic acid of the cell wall

choices.label: E
choices.text: Peptidoglycan of the cell wall

explanation.summary: Lipopolysaccharide is the endotoxin of the gram-negative outer membrane and produces fever, hypotension, bruising, and multiorgan failure.
explanation.whyCorrect: Lipopolysaccharide sits in the outer membrane of gram-negative bacteria and acts as an endotoxin. It activates systemic immune reactions by engaging immune cell receptors such as toll-like receptors, which releases cytokines and other inflammatory mediators. The result is blood vessel dilation and increased permeability, so blood pressure and organ perfusion fall, producing septic shock and potentially multiorgan failure.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Spores are dormant survival structures formed under adverse conditions; by themselves they do not produce shock.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Lipoteichoic acid is an anionic polymer interwoven through the thick wall of gram-positive bacteria, and this patient's isolate is gram-negative.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Mycolic acid is the abundant wall lipid of acid-fast organisms such as Mycobacteria; it accounts for retention of carbol fuchsin, not for endotoxic shock.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Peptidoglycan is the rigid structural exoskeleton that maintains shape and prevents osmotic lysis; it is not the endotoxin described here.

questions.stem: Purified lipopolysaccharide is separated into its three constituent parts, and each part is injected separately into mice. Only one fraction reproduces fever and hypotension. Which of the following parts of the molecule accounts for this effect?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Lipid A

choices.label: B
choices.text: The core polysaccharide

choices.label: C
choices.text: The O antigen

choices.label: D
choices.text: The outer membrane porin

choices.label: E
choices.text: The peptidoglycan cross-link

explanation.summary: Lipopolysaccharide has three parts, and lipid A is the toxic anchor responsible for endotoxin activity.
explanation.whyCorrect: Lipopolysaccharide is composed of lipid A, a core polysaccharide, and an O antigen. Together these provide structural integrity and trigger strong immune responses, but lipid A is specifically the toxic anchor of the molecule. Isolating lipid A therefore reproduces the fever and hypotension of endotoxin exposure.

whyWrongByChoice.B: The core polysaccharide is the middle sugar region that joins the O antigen to lipid A; it is not the toxic moiety.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The O antigen is the outermost carbohydrate portion of lipopolysaccharide and contributes to its structure, not to the toxic activity.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Porins are protein channels that sit in the outer membrane alongside lipopolysaccharide; they are not part of the lipopolysaccharide molecule.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Peptide cross-links belong to peptidoglycan in the cell wall and are unrelated to lipopolysaccharide.

questions.stem: A gram-negative bacillus is cultured in a medium containing a small water-soluble nutrient. Passage of this nutrient inward across the outermost membrane of the organism depends most directly on which of the following structures?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Flagellar filaments

choices.label: B
choices.text: Lipoteichoic acid

choices.label: C
choices.text: Mycolic acid

choices.label: D
choices.text: Peptidoglycan cross-links

choices.label: E
choices.text: Porins

explanation.summary: Porins are the protein channels of the gram-negative outer membrane that allow molecules to cross it.
explanation.whyCorrect: The gram-negative outer membrane is a glycolipid bilayer containing lipopolysaccharide. It also contains porins, protein channels that allow transport of molecules across the membrane. Without porins, a hydrophilic solute could not readily traverse this lipid barrier.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Flagella are elongated protein filaments used for locomotion and chemotaxis, not for nutrient uptake.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Lipoteichoic acid is an anionic polymer unique to the thick cell wall of gram-positive bacteria, which have no outer membrane.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Mycolic acid is a wall lipid of acid-fast organisms and resists decolorization during staining; it is not a transport structure.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Peptidoglycan cross-links give the cell wall strength and shape; they do not form transport channels.

questions.stem: A gram-negative isolate resists ampicillin by producing an enzyme that hydrolyzes the drug before it can reach its target. In this organism, the enzyme is concentrated in which of the following locations?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The basal body that anchors the flagellum

choices.label: B
choices.text: The interior of the peptidoglycan cell wall

choices.label: C
choices.text: The nucleoid at the center of the cytoplasm

choices.label: D
choices.text: The outer leaflet of the outer membrane

choices.label: E
choices.text: The periplasmic space between the two membranes

explanation.summary: Gram-negative bacteria have a periplasmic space between their outer and inner membranes, and this is where beta-lactamase resides.
explanation.whyCorrect: Gram-negative organisms have an outer lipid membrane, a thin cell wall, and an inner lipid membrane. The space between the membranes is the periplasmic space, and it is the location of beta-lactamase. An antibiotic crossing the outer membrane therefore meets the degrading enzyme before it reaches the peptidoglycan it is meant to disrupt.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The basal body anchors the flagellum within the cell wall and plasma membrane and has no role in antibiotic degradation.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The peptidoglycan wall is the target of beta-lactam drugs rather than the compartment where the degrading enzyme is concentrated.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The nucleoid is the central region of the cytoplasm containing the single circular chromosome, not a site of drug-degrading enzymes.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The outer leaflet of the outer membrane carries lipopolysaccharide; beta-lactamase is not situated there.

questions.stem: Two clinical isolates are compared by electron microscopy. Isolate 1 has a thick peptidoglycan layer with anionic polymers interwoven through it and no outer membrane. Isolate 2 has a thin peptidoglycan layer sandwiched between two lipid membranes. Which of the following is found in isolate 1 but not isolate 2?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A plasma membrane

choices.label: B
choices.text: A polysaccharide capsule

choices.label: C
choices.text: Flagella

choices.label: D
choices.text: Lipoteichoic acid

choices.label: E
choices.text: Pili

explanation.summary: Teichoic and lipoteichoic acids are anionic polymers unique to the thick cell wall of gram-positive bacteria.
explanation.whyCorrect: Isolate 1 has the gram-positive envelope: no outer membrane and a much thicker peptidoglycan layer. Teichoic acids and lipoteichoic acids are interwoven throughout that wall and contribute to its strength and stability. Gram-positive organisms also carry surface proteins that serve functions analogous to the periplasmic and outer membrane proteins of gram-negative bacteria.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Both envelopes include a plasma membrane; the gram-negative organism simply has an additional outer membrane.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Capsules occur in some gram-positive and some gram-negative bacteria, so a capsule does not distinguish the two envelopes.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Flagella are common to both gram-positive and gram-negative organisms.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Pili are common to both gram-positive and gram-negative organisms.

questions.stem: Peptidoglycan forms a strong, interconnected network that gives the bacterial cell wall its rigidity and characteristic shape. Which of the following features accounts for this interconnection between adjacent glycan strands?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Disulfide bridges linking adjacent surface proteins

choices.label: B
choices.text: Hydrogen bonds between adjacent porin channels

choices.label: C
choices.text: Hydrophobic stacking of mycolic acid chains

choices.label: D
choices.text: Ionic bridges formed between lipid A anchors

choices.label: E
choices.text: Peptide cross-links extending from N-acetylmuramic acid

explanation.summary: Peptidoglycan strands are joined by short peptide chains attached to N-acetylmuramic acid, creating the cross-linked mesh.
explanation.whyCorrect: Peptidoglycan consists of repeating units of N-acetylglucosamine and N-acetylmuramic acid linked by beta-1,4 glycosidic bonds. A short peptide chain is attached to each N-acetylmuramic acid residue, and these peptides cross-link with neighboring strands. The resulting interconnected network is what gives the wall its strength and shape.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Gram-positive bacteria have surface proteins, but the wall's mesh is built from cross-linked peptides on the glycan backbone, not from protein disulfide bridges.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Porins are transport channels of the gram-negative outer membrane and do not link peptidoglycan strands.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Mycolic acids are found in the walls of acid-fast bacteria and explain retention of carbol fuchsin, not the general architecture of peptidoglycan.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Lipid A is the toxic anchor of lipopolysaccharide in the gram-negative outer membrane and is not part of the peptidoglycan mesh.

questions.stem: Tears and saliva contain an enzyme that lyses many bacteria on contact, and gram-positive organisms are especially susceptible because their cell wall is more exposed. This enzyme acts by which of the following mechanisms?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Binding lipid A and neutralizing endotoxin activity

choices.label: B
choices.text: Blocking nutrient transport through outer membrane porins

choices.label: C
choices.text: Cleaving beta-1,4 linkages between NAG and NAM

choices.label: D
choices.text: Degrading the O antigen of lipopolysaccharide

choices.label: E
choices.text: Inserting pores into the bacterial plasma membrane

explanation.summary: Lysozyme cleaves the beta-1,4 linkages between N-acetylglucosamine and N-acetylmuramic acid, destroying peptidoglycan.
explanation.whyCorrect: Lysozyme is found in tears, saliva, and other body fluids. It breaks the beta-1,4 linkages between N-acetylglucosamine and N-acetylmuramic acid, dismantling peptidoglycan and leading to bacterial cell lysis. Gram-positive bacteria are especially vulnerable because their thick wall is on the outside of the cell rather than buried beneath an outer membrane.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Neutralizing lipid A would blunt endotoxin activity but would not lyse the organism, and gram-positive bacteria do not carry lipopolysaccharide.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Blocking porins would restrict nutrient uptake in gram-negative bacteria; it does not explain lysis of gram-positive organisms.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The O antigen is a lipopolysaccharide component of gram-negative bacteria and is not the substrate of this enzyme.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Lysozyme attacks the peptidoglycan wall; membrane pore formation is not the described mechanism.

questions.stem: A suspension of bacteria is treated with a compound that degrades peptidoglycan and is then placed in a hypotonic solution. Which of the following is the most likely outcome?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The cells become resistant to acid-alcohol decolorization

choices.label: B
choices.text: The cells convert into dormant, heat-resistant spores

choices.label: C
choices.text: The cells shrink as water leaves the cytoplasm

choices.label: D
choices.text: The cells stop translating messenger RNA into protein

choices.label: E
choices.text: The cells swell and lyse from internal cytoplasmic pressure

explanation.summary: The peptidoglycan cell wall is an exoskeleton that prevents osmotic lysis; destroying it causes the cell to burst.
explanation.whyCorrect: The cell wall forms a strong exoskeleton that helps prevent lysis in hypotonic or isotonic solutions and gives bacteria their characteristic shape. If the peptidoglycan is damaged by antibiotics, enzymes, or other compounds, the bacterium lyses from the pressure of its own internal cytoplasm. This is why wall-active agents are bactericidal.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Resistance to acid-alcohol decolorization comes from mycolic acid in the wall of acid-fast organisms and is unrelated to peptidoglycan digestion.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Sporulation is triggered by adverse physiologic conditions such as lack of nutrients, not by enzymatic loss of the wall.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Water moves into the cell in a hypotonic environment, so the cell swells rather than shrinks.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Translation occurs on free ribosomes in the cytoplasm and is not the immediate consequence of removing the wall.

questions.stem: Two motile gram-negative rods are compared by electron microscopy. The first bears a single flagellum at one pole, as in Pseudomonas aeruginosa. The second bears flagella distributed over its entire surface. The arrangement seen in the second organism is best described by which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Clustered, as in Staphylococcus species

choices.label: B
choices.text: Diploid, as in Neisseria species

choices.label: C
choices.text: Hyphal, as in Nocardia species

choices.label: D
choices.text: Peritrichous, as in Salmonella species

choices.label: E
choices.text: Polar, as in Pseudomonas species

explanation.summary: Flagella arranged all around the bacterium are peritrichous, as in Salmonella; a flagellum at one or both ends is polar, as in Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
explanation.whyCorrect: Flagella are elongated protein filament cylinders anchored inside the cell wall and plasma membrane, and their whip-like motion propels the bacterium. Their arrangement is useful in identification: they may sit at one or both ends, which is polar, or all around the cell, which is peritrichous. Salmonella species are the example given for the peritrichous pattern.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Clustering describes bacteria that bunch together like grapes, such as Staphylococcus, and is also a grouping pattern.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Diploid describes bacteria that form pairs, such as Neisseria, and is a grouping pattern rather than a flagellar arrangement.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Hyphae are long thread-like filaments formed by grouped bacteria such as Nocardia; this is a grouping pattern, not a flagellar arrangement.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Polar describes the first organism, with a flagellum at one end, and does not describe surface-wide distribution.

questions.stem: A gram-negative rod colonizes the human intestinal lining using numerous tiny hair-like surface projections that carry proteins and glycoproteins capable of binding host surfaces. These projections serve which of the following primary functions?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Adhesion to host cells

choices.label: B
choices.text: Antibiotic resistance

choices.label: C
choices.text: Defense against predators

choices.label: D
choices.text: Ingestion of nutrients

choices.label: E
choices.text: Motility

explanation.summary: Pili and fimbriae carry adhesins and function primarily in adhesion to surfaces and host tissue.
explanation.whyCorrect: Pili, also called fimbriae, appear as tiny hairs around a bacterium. They often bear adhesins, proteins or glycoproteins that play an integral role in attachment, allowing the organism to stick to environmental surfaces or to other organisms such as the human intestinal lining. Adhesion is their principal function.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Fimbriae have no known role in antibiotic resistance itself, although larger fimbriae can transfer resistance genes during conjugation.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Fimbriae have no known role in defending the organism against predators.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Fimbriae have no known role in the ingestion or uptake of nutrients.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Motility is the function of flagella, whose whip-like motion propels the bacterium.

questions.stem: An Escherichia coli isolate acquires a drug resistance determinant from a neighboring bacterial cell during direct cell-to-cell contact. Which of the following bacterial structures mediates this transfer?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Chromosomal nucleoid

choices.label: B
choices.text: Flagellar filament

choices.label: C
choices.text: Larger fimbria (R-pilus)

choices.label: D
choices.text: Outer membrane porin

choices.label: E
choices.text: Polysaccharide capsule

explanation.summary: Larger fimbriae, known as R-pili, carry out drug resistance transfer during bacterial conjugation.
explanation.whyCorrect: Pili and fimbriae are the tiny hair-like appendages that normally mediate adhesion. The larger fimbriae, also called R-pili, are specifically involved in drug resistance transfer by bacterial conjugation, in which genetic material moves between cells in direct contact. This is one way resistance spreads within a bacterial population.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The nucleoid is the cytoplasmic region holding the circular chromosome; it is the source of DNA, not the structure that transfers it.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Flagella propel the bacterium and allow it to respond to chemical gradients; they do not transfer genetic material.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Porins are transport channels for molecules crossing the gram-negative outer membrane, not a conjugation apparatus.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The capsule is a polysaccharide layer that protects against phagocytosis and does not mediate gene transfer.

questions.stem: A newly isolated single-celled organism is examined by electron microscopy. It has a cell wall, free ribosomes, and a central region of condensed DNA, but no nuclear membrane. Which of the following additional findings is most likely?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A Golgi apparatus adjacent to the plasma membrane

choices.label: B
choices.text: Linear chromosomes containing non-expressed introns

choices.label: C
choices.text: Mitochondria supplying the cell with energy

choices.label: D
choices.text: No membrane-bound organelles and no cytoskeleton

choices.label: E
choices.text: Rough endoplasmic reticulum studded with ribosomes

explanation.summary: Prokaryotes lack a nucleus, membrane-bound organelles, and a cytoskeleton; their DNA sits in a nucleoid within the cytoplasm.
explanation.whyCorrect: The findings described are those of a prokaryote: a cell wall, free ribosomes, and a nucleoid holding the chromosome, with no nuclear membrane. Prokaryotes do not have a nucleus, membrane-bound organelles, or a cytoskeleton. Metabolic processes that eukaryotes carry out in organelles are instead relegated to the inner membrane.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The Golgi apparatus is a membrane-bound organelle found in eukaryotic cells and is absent from prokaryotes.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The bacterial chromosome is circular, without free ends of DNA, and does not contain introns.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Mitochondria are membrane-bound eukaryotic organelles and are not present in prokaryotic cells.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Bacteria have free ribosomes but no endoplasmic reticulum, which is a membranous eukaryotic organelle.

questions.stem: An investigational antimicrobial binds sterols within the plasma membrane. When it is tested against a panel of bacterial isolates, nearly all are unaffected, but organisms of one genus are readily killed. That genus is most likely which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Clostridium

choices.label: B
choices.text: Mycoplasma

choices.label: C
choices.text: Nocardia

choices.label: D
choices.text: Salmonella

choices.label: E
choices.text: Staphylococcus

explanation.summary: Mycoplasma species are the notable exception to the rule that bacterial cytoplasmic membranes contain no sterols.
explanation.whyCorrect: The bacterial cytoplasmic membrane closely resembles the eukaryotic cell membrane, with one key structural difference: the vast majority of bacterial membranes contain no sterols, unlike the cholesterol of human membranes or the ergosterol of fungal membranes. The most notable exception to this lack of sterols is the genus Mycoplasma, including Mycoplasma pneumoniae. A sterol-binding agent would therefore act selectively on Mycoplasma.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Clostridium species are spore-forming organisms whose cytoplasmic membrane, like that of most bacteria, lacks sterols.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Nocardia is distinguished by mycolic acids in its cell wall, which make it acid fast; its membrane is sterol free.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Salmonella species are ordinary gram-negative rods whose cytoplasmic membrane contains no sterols.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Staphylococcus species have a thick gram-positive wall and a sterol-free cytoplasmic membrane.

questions.stem: An organism recovered from an intra-abdominal abscess fails to grow when its plate is incubated in room air but grows well inside an anaerobic chamber. Lack of which of the following best explains this growth pattern?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Beta-lactamase and outer membrane porins

choices.label: B
choices.text: DNA polymerase and DNA ligase

choices.label: C
choices.text: Lysozyme and salivary peptidases

choices.label: D
choices.text: Superoxide dismutase and catalase

choices.label: E
choices.text: Transferrin and lactoferrin

explanation.summary: Obligate anaerobes cannot survive in oxygen because they lack superoxide dismutase and catalase.
explanation.whyCorrect: Oxygen is toxic to obligate anaerobes. They cannot live in an oxygen atmosphere because they lack superoxide dismutase and catalase, the enzymes that protect other bacteria from oxygen free radicals. Deprived of that protection, the organism grows only when oxygen is excluded.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Beta-lactamase confers antibiotic resistance and porins are transport channels; neither relates to oxygen tolerance.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Enzymes of DNA replication are required by all bacteria regardless of their oxygen requirements.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Lysozyme is a host enzyme found in tears and saliva that attacks bacterial peptidoglycan; bacteria are not expected to produce it.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Transferrin and lactoferrin are host iron-binding proteins, not bacterial enzymes, and they restrict iron rather than oxygen.

questions.stem: A patient with an anaerobic soft tissue infection is treated with metronidazole, an agent chosen because it exploits a metabolic vulnerability that is specific to obligate anaerobes. That vulnerability is best described as which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Absence of sterols from the cytoplasmic membrane

choices.label: B
choices.text: Dependence on host transferrin as an iron source

choices.label: C
choices.text: Inability to detoxify oxygen-derived free radicals

choices.label: D
choices.text: Inability to form spores when nutrients are scarce

choices.label: E
choices.text: Reliance on binary fission rather than budding

explanation.summary: Metronidazole exploits the obligate anaerobe's inability to handle oxygen free radicals, the metabolic Achilles heel of these organisms.
explanation.whyCorrect: Obligate anaerobes lack superoxide dismutase and catalase and therefore cannot protect themselves from oxygen free radicals. Some antibiotics, metronidazole among them, are used precisely because they exploit this metabolic Achilles heel. The defect is specific to obligate anaerobes, which is why the drug is targeted at anaerobic infection.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Nearly all bacteria lack membrane sterols, with Mycoplasma the notable exception, so this does not single out anaerobes.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Competition for host-bound iron is a general feature of pathogenic bacteria, not a property unique to obligate anaerobes.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Many obligate anaerobes, including Clostridium species, do form spores under adverse conditions, so this is not their defining weakness.
whyWrongByChoice.E: All clinically important bacteria replicate by binary fission, so this cannot explain selective activity against anaerobes.

questions.stem: A gram-negative rod recovered from urine grows on a plate incubated in room air and also in an anaerobic jar, switching between aerobic respiration and anaerobic fermentation depending on conditions. This organism is best classified as which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Acid-fast organism

choices.label: B
choices.text: Facultative anaerobe

choices.label: C
choices.text: Fastidious organism

choices.label: D
choices.text: Obligate aerobe

choices.label: E
choices.text: Obligate anaerobe

explanation.summary: Facultative anaerobes grow in both oxygen-rich and oxygen-free conditions by switching between respiration and fermentation.
explanation.whyCorrect: Bacteria are grouped into three broad categories by oxygen requirement: obligate aerobes, obligate anaerobes, and facultative anaerobes. Facultative organisms are well adapted to both oxygen-rich and oxygen-free environments and can switch between aerobic respiration and anaerobic fermentation. That flexibility is exactly what this isolate demonstrates.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Acid fast describes a staining property conferred by mycolic acids and says nothing about oxygen requirements.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Fastidious describes an organism that grows only when specific nutrients are supplied; it is not a category of oxygen requirement.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Obligate aerobes require oxygen for survival and growth and would not grow in the anaerobic jar.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Oxygen is toxic to obligate anaerobes, so this organism would not grow on the aerobic plate.

questions.stem: A respiratory isolate will not grow on standard agar, but it grows readily when the medium is enriched with blood and the plate is incubated in a carbon dioxide-rich atmosphere. This organism is best described by which of the following terms?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Acid fast

choices.label: B
choices.text: Competent

choices.label: C
choices.text: Facultative

choices.label: D
choices.text: Fastidious

choices.label: E
choices.text: Peritrichous

explanation.summary: Fastidious bacteria are the picky eaters that grow only when specific nutrients, such as blood iron or carbon dioxide, are supplied.
explanation.whyCorrect: Fastidious organisms will grow only when particular nutrients are present, such as the iron in human blood or a carbon dioxide-rich environment. Failure on plain agar with good growth on enriched medium in a carbon dioxide atmosphere is the classic laboratory behavior of such an organism. The term describes nutritional requirements rather than oxygen tolerance.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Acid fast describes retention of carbol fuchsin after acid-alcohol washing, a staining property.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Competent describes a bacterium able to absorb naked DNA from the environment and integrate it into its chromosome.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Facultative describes an organism that grows with or without oxygen and says nothing about nutrient enrichment.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Peritrichous describes flagella distributed over the entire surface of the bacterium, a morphologic feature.

questions.stem: Free iron is extremely scarce in human blood and tissues because it is bound by proteins such as transferrin, lactoferrin, and ceruloplasmin. Pathogenic bacteria that require free iron most often overcome this restriction by which of the following strategies?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Excreting chelating compounds that bind and capture iron

choices.label: B
choices.text: Forming spores that persist until iron becomes available

choices.label: C
choices.text: Importing host iron-binding proteins through their porins

choices.label: D
choices.text: Storing iron in transient granules before invading tissue

choices.label: E
choices.text: Switching to fermentation so that iron is not required

explanation.summary: Bacteria that need free iron secrete chelating compounds that bind iron and effectively steal it from host proteins.
explanation.whyCorrect: Virtually all bacterial species require nutrients such as iron, magnesium, and zinc. Because host proteins keep free iron extremely scarce, pathogenic bacteria that depend on it excrete chelating compounds that bind iron, essentially stealing it from blood and tissue proteins. This is a core strategy for surviving inside the host.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Sporulation is a dormancy response to adverse physiologic conditions, not a mechanism for acquiring iron from host proteins.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Porins allow small molecules to cross the outer membrane; importing intact host iron-binding proteins is not the described mechanism.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Some bacteria carry transient cytoplasmic granules, but storing iron does not solve the problem of obtaining it from host proteins.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Iron is a nutrient requirement of virtually all bacteria and is needed whether the organism respires or ferments.

questions.stem: A blood agar plate inoculated with a clinical isolate shows clearing of the red cells surrounding each colony. The principal benefit of this hemolytic activity to the bacterium is which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Creation of a chemical gradient that guides motility

choices.label: B
choices.text: Neutralization of host antibody bound to its surface

choices.label: C
choices.text: Prevention of phagocyte attachment to the cell wall

choices.label: D
choices.text: Protection of the cell wall from attack by lysozyme

choices.label: E
choices.text: Release of iron and other nutrients needed for growth

explanation.summary: Hemolysins lyse red blood cells so the bacterium can obtain the iron and nutrients they contain.
explanation.whyCorrect: Because free iron is bound by host proteins and is scarce in blood and tissue, it is very common for bacteria to be hemolytic, possessing toxins that lyse red blood cells. Destroying erythrocytes liberates the iron and other nutrients inside them for bacterial use. Hemolysis is therefore primarily a nutrient acquisition strategy.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Chemotaxis is the movement of bacteria toward or away from chemicals in the environment and is mediated by flagella.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Lysing red blood cells does not neutralize antibody, and antibody evasion is not the described purpose of hemolysins.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Protection from phagocytosis is the primary function of the polysaccharide capsule, not of hemolytic toxins.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Protection from lysozyme is not conferred by hemolysis; lysozyme acts on the peptidoglycan of the cell wall.

questions.stem: A bacterial population becomes resistant to an antibiotic after taking up free DNA released into the medium by lysed cells and integrating it into its own chromosome by homologous recombination. Bacteria able to do this are described as which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Competent

choices.label: B
choices.text: Fastidious

choices.label: C
choices.text: Hemolytic

choices.label: D
choices.text: Microaerophilic

choices.label: E
choices.text: Peritrichous

explanation.summary: Competent bacteria absorb naked DNA from the environment and integrate it by homologous recombination, one of the routes to antimicrobial resistance.
explanation.whyCorrect: Bacterial generational time is brief, and rapid growth allows quick adaptation to a changing host environment. Some bacteria, termed competent, can absorb naked DNA from the environment and integrate it into the bacterial chromosome through homologous recombination. This is one of the three mechanisms by which many bacteria gain antimicrobial resistance.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Fastidious describes organisms that grow only when specific nutrients such as blood iron or carbon dioxide are supplied.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Hemolytic describes organisms that produce toxins lysing red blood cells to obtain iron and nutrients.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Microaerophilic describes organisms sometimes grouped with facultative anaerobes on the basis of oxygen requirements.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Peritrichous describes flagella distributed over the whole bacterial surface and has nothing to do with DNA uptake.

questions.stem: Bacteria that cause human infections replicate by a process in which the chromosome of a single bacterium is first duplicated, after which the cytoplasm divides into two equally sized daughter cells. This process is called which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Binary fission

choices.label: B
choices.text: Chemotaxis

choices.label: C
choices.text: Conjugation

choices.label: D
choices.text: Sporulation

choices.label: E
choices.text: Transformation

explanation.summary: Binary fission, in which a replicated chromosome is followed by equal division of the cytoplasm, is how clinically important bacteria reproduce.
explanation.whyCorrect: Binary fission is clinically the most important form of bacterial reproduction, because bacteria that cause human infections replicate only by this method. The chromosome of a single bacterium is replicated, and then the cytoplasm divides into two equally sized daughter cells. Because each cell yields two, the population multiplies exponentially.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Chemotaxis is movement toward or away from chemicals in the environment and is unrelated to replication.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Conjugation transfers genetic material between cells in direct contact and does not by itself produce new cells.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Sporulation is the formation of dormant structures under adverse conditions, not a means of population growth.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Transformation is the uptake of naked DNA from the environment by competent bacteria.

questions.stem: An organism recovered from improperly processed canned food survives boiling, prolonged drying, and exposure to chemical disinfectants, then resumes active growth when placed in fresh broth. Which of the following best explains this resilience?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A polysaccharide capsule surrounding its cell wall

choices.label: B
choices.text: A thick layer of mycolic acid within its cell wall

choices.label: C
choices.text: Formation of dormant spores under adverse conditions

choices.label: D
choices.text: Loss of the peptidoglycan wall during environmental stress

choices.label: E
choices.text: Production of enzymes that degrade the disinfectant

explanation.summary: Under adverse conditions some bacteria form spores, dormant structures that withstand heat, radiation, desiccation, and disinfectants.
explanation.whyCorrect: In the presence of adverse physiologic conditions such as lack of nutrients, some bacteria transform into spores. These dormant structures last a long time and withstand extreme environmental stresses including disinfectants, radiation, high temperatures, and desiccation. Spores reactivate when the environment becomes favorable again, and they are an essential way that organisms such as Bacillus and Clostridium reach humans.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The capsule protects the organism from phagocytosis in the host; it does not confer resistance to boiling or desiccation.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Mycolic acid in the wall of acid-fast organisms explains retention of carbol fuchsin after acid-alcohol washing, not survival of sterilizing conditions.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Losing the peptidoglycan wall removes the exoskeleton that prevents lysis and would make the organism more fragile, not more resistant.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Enzymatic degradation of disinfectants is not the described mechanism of environmental survival in these organisms.

questions.stem: A 4-month-old girl is brought in for a 3-day history of constipation followed by poor feeding, drooling, a weak cry, and a flat facial expression. Her parents mention that they recently began dipping her pacifier in honey. Which of the following best explains her illness?

choices.label: A
choices.text: An acid-fast organism invading the intestinal mucosa

choices.label: B
choices.text: Endotoxin released as gram-negative bacteria lyse in the gut

choices.label: C
choices.text: Exponential growth of a fastidious organism in the blood

choices.label: D
choices.text: Spores germinating in the gut and producing a paralytic toxin

choices.label: E
choices.text: Transfer of a resistance plasmid between gut organisms

explanation.summary: Clostridium botulinum spores in honey germinate in the immature infant gut and release botulinum toxin, producing constipation and descending paralysis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Spores of Clostridium botulinum can contaminate honey. Infants have immature digestive systems that cannot handle and clear the spores, so the spores germinate in the gut and produce toxin, causing infant botulism. Constipation from paralysis of the gut is the first sign parents usually notice, followed by respiratory distress, lack of facial expression, excessive drooling, and muscle weakness from the paralytic effects of botulinum toxin.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Acid-fast organisms are distinguished by mycolic acids in their walls and are not the source of this toxin-mediated syndrome.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Endotoxin from gram-negative bacteria produces fever, hypotension, bruising, and organ failure rather than constipation and flaccid weakness.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Fastidious organisms are defined by their nutrient requirements in culture, and bloodstream growth would not explain a descending paralysis beginning with constipation.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Conjugative transfer of resistance genes changes antibiotic susceptibility and does not produce a paralytic illness.

questions.stem: Bacteria from an overnight culture are inoculated into fresh broth. Over the first several hours the cells mature and adapt to the new medium, but the number of viable organisms increases very little. This interval corresponds to which of the following phases of the growth curve?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Death phase

choices.label: B
choices.text: Exponential growth phase

choices.label: C
choices.text: Lag phase

choices.label: D
choices.text: Period of convalescence

choices.label: E
choices.text: Stationary phase

explanation.summary: In the lag phase bacteria mature and adapt to the growth environment, so reproduction is slow.
explanation.whyCorrect: Bacterial growth in culture has four distinct phases. In the lag phase, bacteria mature and adapt to the growth environment, and as a result reproduction is slow and the viable count changes little. Only once adaptation is complete does the culture enter rapid growth.

whyWrongByChoice.A: In the death phase the bacterial population diminishes and eventually dies out.
whyWrongByChoice.B: In the exponential growth phase the population expands rapidly, with new cells produced in proportion to the number already present.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The period of convalescence is a stage of the clinical course of an infection, not a phase of the culture growth curve.
whyWrongByChoice.E: In the stationary phase the total count plateaus because new bacteria appearing and bacteria dying are roughly equal.

questions.stem: During one interval of a bacterial culture's growth, the number of new cells produced is proportional to the number of bacteria present at that moment, and the population doubles repeatedly. This interval continues until which of the following occurs?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Dormant spores begin to germinate in the culture

choices.label: B
choices.text: Host antibody is generated against the organism

choices.label: C
choices.text: The culture is shifted to an anaerobic atmosphere

choices.label: D
choices.text: The culture runs out of nutrients or physical space

choices.label: E
choices.text: The inoculum finishes adapting to the new medium

explanation.summary: Exponential growth continues until the bacteria exhaust resources such as nutrients or physical space.
explanation.whyCorrect: The exponential growth phase is the period of rapid bacterial growth, during which the number of new cells created is proportional to the number of bacteria present at a given time. Because each cell divides into two, the population rises as 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, and so on. This phase continues until the bacteria run out of resources such as physical space or nutrients, after which the culture plateaus.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Spore germination occurs when conditions become favorable again and is not what halts rapid growth.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Host immunity is a factor in human infection rather than an event that ends exponential growth in a broth culture.
whyWrongByChoice.C: A shift in oxygen tension affects which organisms can grow at all but is not the described limit on exponential growth.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Adaptation to the medium happens during the lag phase, which precedes rather than terminates exponential growth.

questions.stem: A broth culture reaches a point at which the number of new bacteria appearing and the number dying are roughly equal, so the total viable count no longer changes. Which of the following best accounts for this plateau?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A switch from binary fission to sexual reproduction

choices.label: B
choices.text: Conversion of the whole population into dormant spores

choices.label: C
choices.text: Depletion of nutrients, toxic waste, or lack of space

choices.label: D
choices.text: Loss of the peptidoglycan wall from lysozyme exposure

choices.label: E
choices.text: Spread of resistance plasmids throughout the population

explanation.summary: The stationary phase reflects a physiologic limit on growth: nutrients run out, toxic waste accumulates, or space is exhausted.
explanation.whyCorrect: During the stationary phase a physiologic limitation to growth has been reached. This includes lack of available nutrients, accumulation of toxic waste material, or lack of available space. Total growth is stationary because the number of new bacteria appearing and the number dying are roughly the same.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Bacteria reproduce asexually by binary fission; there is no switch to sexual reproduction.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Sporulation is a response to adverse conditions in some genera, but the plateau is defined by balanced growth and death, not by universal dormancy.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Lysozyme digests peptidoglycan and lyses bacteria outright; it does not create a balanced plateau of growth and death.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Transfer of resistance genes alters antibiotic susceptibility and does not determine the shape of the growth curve.

questions.stem: In an untreated human infection the number of colony-forming units eventually falls and the bacterial population dies out. Beyond nutrient depletion and accumulation of waste, which of the following most often drives this decline within the host?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A change in the organism's Gram-staining reaction

choices.label: B
choices.text: Conversion of the organisms to an acid-fast state

choices.label: C
choices.text: Loss of flagella and the resulting loss of motility

choices.label: D
choices.text: Spontaneous reversion of the culture to lag phase

choices.label: E
choices.text: The host immune response against the organism

explanation.summary: In vivo, the death phase of a bacterial population is driven in large part by the host immune response.
explanation.whyCorrect: The death phase is the period when the bacterial population diminishes and eventually dies. In culture this reflects nutrient exhaustion, waste accumulation, and lack of space. In the case of infections in humans, the host immune response is an additional and often decisive cause of the decline, which is mirrored clinically by the period of decline and convalescence.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Gram reaction reflects the structure of the cell envelope and does not change in a way that kills off the population.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Acid fastness is a fixed property of organisms with mycolic acid in their walls; bacteria do not convert to that state to explain population decline.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Loss of motility would limit spread but is not the described cause of the falling colony count.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The lag phase occurs at the start of growth in a new environment and is not a state the population reverts into as it dies.

questions.stem: A 19-year-old college student develops fever, headache, and neck stiffness over about 36 hours and deteriorates rapidly; gram-negative diplococci are seen in the cerebrospinal fluid. A second patient has 3 months of cough, night sweats, and weight loss caused by an organism that divides roughly once every 24 hours. Which of the following best explains the difference in tempo between these two illnesses?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Only the faster organism possesses a polysaccharide capsule

choices.label: B
choices.text: Only the slower organism is able to form dormant spores

choices.label: C
choices.text: The generation time of the organism sets the pace of illness

choices.label: D
choices.text: The slower organism grows only as an obligate anaerobe

choices.label: E
choices.text: The two organisms reach the host by different routes

explanation.summary: How fast an organism divides determines how fast the illness evolves, from hyperacute meningococcal meningitis to chronic tuberculosis.
explanation.whyCorrect: The explosiveness of exponential growth means even a small number of bacteria can rapidly initiate invasive infection after a short prodrome. Neisseria meningitidis divides at least once per hour in cerebrospinal fluid, so the physician must intervene with great speed to avoid a fatal outcome in acute meningococcal meningitis. Mycobacteria such as M. tuberculosis divide only about every 24 hours, so their period of illness is chronic and takes considerable time to manifest.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Capsules protect against phagocytosis but do not determine how quickly the organism divides or how fast the illness progresses.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Spore formation is described for Bacillus and Clostridium; it is not the feature distinguishing these two organisms or the reason for their tempo.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Oxygen requirement describes where an organism can grow, not the speed of its replication or the pace of disease.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The route by which an organism reaches the host does not set the rate at which its population expands once infection is established.

questions.stem: A technician performs a Gram stain on cerebrospinal fluid. After the crystal violet dye is applied to the smear, which of the following gives the correct order of the remaining steps?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A decolorizing agent, then iodide, then safranin

choices.label: B
choices.text: A decolorizing agent, then safranin, then iodide

choices.label: C
choices.text: Iodide, then a decolorizing agent, then safranin

choices.label: D
choices.text: Iodide, then safranin, then a decolorizing agent

choices.label: E
choices.text: Safranin, then iodide, then a decolorizing agent

explanation.summary: The Gram stain runs crystal violet, then iodide, then a decolorizing agent, then a safranin counterstain.
explanation.whyCorrect: Crystal violet dye is applied first, followed by iodide, which binds to the violet dye. A decolorizing agent is then applied, and finally a pink counterstain such as safranin is added. Thick gram-positive walls retain the crystal violet and iodide complex through decolorization and appear deep purple, while gram-negative organisms lose it and take up only the safranin, appearing pink or red.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Decolorizing before the iodide is added means no dye-iodide complex has formed, so gram-positive organisms would not retain the violet color.
whyWrongByChoice.B: This order both decolorizes before the complex forms and ends with iodide rather than with the counterstain.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Counterstaining before decolorization would defeat the purpose of the decolorizing step, which must select which cells keep the violet complex.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Applying the pink counterstain first would color all cells before the violet complex could be selectively retained or removed.

questions.stem: On a Gram stain of sputum, some organisms appear deep purple while others appear pink. The purple organisms retain the crystal violet and iodide complex for which of the following reasons?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Their cell membrane is thicker and so holds the dye

choices.label: B
choices.text: Their wall components bind the dye more tightly

choices.label: C
choices.text: They have a thick cell wall that traps the dye

choices.label: D
choices.text: They lack enzymes capable of degrading the violet dye

choices.label: E
choices.text: They possess two lipid membranes that trap the dye

explanation.summary: Gram-positive bacteria stain purple because their thick peptidoglycan wall holds the crystal violet and iodide complex through decolorization.
explanation.whyCorrect: Gram-positive bacteria have thick peptidoglycan cell walls. These hefty walls retain the crystal violet and iodide complex even after the decolorizing agent is applied, so the organisms end up deep purple or blue. Gram-negative bacteria lose the complex and retain only the safranin counterstain, which is why they appear pink or red.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Cell membrane thickness does not vary widely between gram-positive and gram-negative organisms; the difference lies in the wall.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Gram-positive and gram-negative walls have the same basic composition, primarily peptidoglycan, so binding affinity is not what differs.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The Gram stain dye is not known to be degraded by any bacterial enzyme, so enzymatic destruction does not explain the color difference.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Two membrane layers are a gram-negative feature, and those organisms are the ones that lose the violet complex and appear pink.

questions.stem: The average bacterium is approximately 1 micrometer long, compared with about 7.5 micrometers for a mature human red blood cell. This compact size contributes to bacterial metabolic efficiency primarily because it does which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Allows the cell to evade host phagocytic cells

choices.label: B
choices.text: Eliminates the cell's requirement for a rigid wall

choices.label: C
choices.text: Gives the cell a high surface-to-volume ratio

choices.label: D
choices.text: Permits storage of large reserves of nutrients

choices.label: E
choices.text: Removes the need for ribosomes in the cytoplasm

explanation.summary: Being roughly 1 micrometer across gives bacteria a high surface-to-volume ratio, which minimizes the energy cost of nutrient transport.
explanation.whyCorrect: Bacteria are generally small, with an average length of about 1 micrometer against roughly 7.5 micrometers for a human red blood cell. This compact size means no part of the cytoplasm is distant from the cell wall, giving a high surface-to-volume ratio. With that configuration, the energy costs of transporting nutrients are minimized, which contributes to metabolic efficiency.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Evasion of phagocytosis is attributed to the polysaccharide capsule, not to the organism's small dimensions.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Bacteria still need a rigid peptidoglycan wall to maintain shape and prevent osmotic lysis regardless of their small size.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Small size limits rather than expands the room available for storing nutrient reserves.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Bacteria retain free ribosomes in the cytoplasm because they still must translate messenger RNA into protein.

questions.stem: Sputum from a patient with a chronic cough is stained with carbol fuchsin and then washed with acid alcohol. Slender bright red bacilli stand out against a blue counterstained background. The property allowing these organisms to retain the red dye is which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A polysaccharide capsule around the wall

choices.label: B
choices.text: A thick outer layer of peptidoglycan

choices.label: C
choices.text: Large amounts of mycolic acid within the wall

choices.label: D
choices.text: Lipopolysaccharide within an outer membrane

choices.label: E
choices.text: Teichoic acids interwoven through the wall

explanation.summary: Acid-fast organisms retain carbol fuchsin after acid-alcohol washing because their cell walls contain large amounts of mycolic acids.
explanation.whyCorrect: Acid-fast staining, also called Ziehl-Neelsen or carbol fuchsin staining, differentiates atypical bacteria, especially Mycobacteria and Nocardia, which are Gram nonreactive and retain no dye from the Gram stain. Carbol fuchsin initially stains all cells, but after washing with acid alcohol only acid-fast bacteria keep the bright red color, because large amounts of mycolic acids in their cell walls resist decolorization. The background and other cells are counterstained with methylene blue.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Capsules do not bind most dyes and are demonstrated by staining the background with India ink or nigrosine instead.
whyWrongByChoice.B: A thick peptidoglycan layer explains retention of crystal violet in the Gram stain, not resistance to acid-alcohol decolorization.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Lipopolysaccharide is the endotoxin of the gram-negative outer membrane and does not confer acid fastness.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Teichoic acids are anionic polymers of the gram-positive cell wall and do not resist acid-alcohol washing.

questions.stem: To demonstrate the capsule of an encapsulated isolate, a laboratory suspends the organisms in India ink before examining the slide. Clear halos appear around each cell. This appearance occurs because of which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Acid alcohol strips the ink from the capsule

choices.label: B
choices.text: The capsule fluoresces when the ink is illuminated

choices.label: C
choices.text: The ink is taken up selectively by the capsule

choices.label: D
choices.text: The ink precipitates onto the peptidoglycan wall

choices.label: E
choices.text: The ink stains the background but not the capsule

explanation.summary: Capsules are demonstrated by negative staining: the background is stained with India ink or nigrosine, leaving the capsule as a clear halo.
explanation.whyCorrect: Because capsules do not bind to most dyes, they are visualized indirectly by staining the background, most commonly with India ink or nigrosine. The bacteria themselves can be counterstained while the capsule remains clear. The end result is bacteria surrounded by clear halos against a dark field.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Acid alcohol is the decolorizing step of acid-fast staining and plays no part in visualizing capsules.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Fluorescence is not the mechanism described; the halo is simply an unstained region against a stained background.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The capsule does not bind most dyes, which is precisely why a direct stain fails and a negative stain is used.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The ink does not deposit on the cell wall; it colors the surrounding field while the cell and its capsule stand out against it.

questions.stem: A microbiology report describes an organism seen on a stained smear as curved and comma-like. This description corresponds to which of the following bacterial shapes?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Bacillus

choices.label: B
choices.text: Coccobacillus

choices.label: C
choices.text: Coccus

choices.label: D
choices.text: Spirochete

choices.label: E
choices.text: Vibrio

explanation.summary: A vibrio is a curved, comma-shaped bacterium.
explanation.whyCorrect: Besides Gram reactivity, bacteria are classified by shape. A vibrio has a curved, comma-like shape, which is exactly what is described here. Recognizing the shape narrows the differential before culture results return.

whyWrongByChoice.A: A bacillus is an elongated rod, described as being shaped like a hot dog.
whyWrongByChoice.B: A coccobacillus is intermediate between cocci and bacilli and looks like a short rod or an oval.
whyWrongByChoice.C: A coccus is spherical in shape rather than curved.
whyWrongByChoice.D: A spirochete has a twisted shape, like the threads on a screw.

questions.stem: A Gram stain of pus aspirated from a skin abscess shows gram-positive cocci bunched together in irregular, grape-like groups. This grouping pattern is characteristic of which of the following genera?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Neisseria

choices.label: B
choices.text: Nocardia

choices.label: C
choices.text: Salmonella

choices.label: D
choices.text: Staphylococcus

choices.label: E
choices.text: Streptococcus

explanation.summary: Bacteria that bunch together like grapes are clusters, the grouping pattern of Staphylococcus.
explanation.whyCorrect: Besides shape and Gram reactivity, bacteria are classified by their grouping patterns. Clusters are bacteria that bunch together like grapes, and Staphylococcus is the example given for this arrangement. Gram-positive cocci in grape-like clusters from an abscess therefore point to this genus.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Neisseria forms diploids, meaning pairs, and is gram negative rather than gram positive.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Nocardia forms hyphae, long thread-like filaments, and is not a coccus.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Salmonella is a flagellated rod, not a gram-positive coccus arranged in clusters.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Streptococcus forms chains, which are short single-file lines of cocci rather than irregular clusters.

questions.stem: A laboratory is characterizing the genetic material of a clinical Escherichia coli isolate. Which of the following best describes the typical organization of this organism's chromosomal genome?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A single circular molecule of double-stranded DNA

choices.label: B
choices.text: A single circular molecule of single-stranded RNA

choices.label: C
choices.text: A single linear chromosome paired with a homologous copy

choices.label: D
choices.text: Multiple linear chromosomes enclosed by a nuclear membrane

choices.label: E
choices.text: Several circular chromosomes present in two copies each

explanation.summary: The bacterial genome is typically one circular, double-stranded DNA chromosome.
explanation.whyCorrect: Bacteria are prokaryotes whose genome is typically a single, circular chromosome made of DNA. Replication of that molecule yields two identical circular double-stranded chromosomes. Additional DNA may be carried extrachromosomally in plasmids or in integrated viral DNA, but the chromosome itself is a single circular molecule.

whyWrongByChoice.B: The bacterial genome is DNA; single-stranded RNA genomes belong to certain viruses.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Bacterial DNA is haploid and circular, so there is no paired linear homolog.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Prokaryotes have no nuclear membrane, and the chromosome is not a set of linear molecules.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Bacteria carry one set of chromosomal DNA; they do not maintain duplicate chromosome sets.

questions.stem: A hospital isolate carries a segment of DNA that lies outside the chromosome, replicates on its own schedule, and most often encodes antibiotic resistance. This element is best described as which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A plasmid

choices.label: B
choices.text: A prophage

choices.label: C
choices.text: A ribosome

choices.label: D
choices.text: A sex pilus

choices.label: E
choices.text: A transposon

explanation.summary: Plasmids are circular extrachromosomal DNA molecules that replicate independently and usually carry resistance genes.
explanation.whyCorrect: Plasmids are independent of the bacterial genome and replicate independently of it. They most often contain genes encoding antibiotic resistance, and being extrachromosomal facilitates their ease of transfer between cells. Conjugation moves such plasmids from one bacterium to another.

whyWrongByChoice.B: A prophage is viral DNA integrated into the host chromosome, not an independently replicating resistance element.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The ribosome is the 70S protein-synthesis machine of the cell, not a DNA element.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The sex pilus is a surface appendage encoded by the F plasmid, not a DNA molecule.
whyWrongByChoice.E: A transposon is a DNA sequence that jumps within a genome; it is not a self-replicating extrachromosomal element.

questions.stem: A student notes that bacterial genetics lacks the dominant and recessive allele relationships seen in human genetics. Which feature of bacterial cells best explains this?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Their DNA is copied by a polymerase that proofreads each strand

choices.label: B
choices.text: Their DNA is haploid, so only one set of chromosome is present

choices.label: C
choices.text: Their DNA is packaged inside a membrane-bound nuclear compartment

choices.label: D
choices.text: Their DNA is rebuilt from two parent cells at every division

choices.label: E
choices.text: Their DNA is transcribed but is never translated into protein

explanation.summary: Bacterial DNA is haploid, with only one set of chromosome, because bacteria divide clonally.
explanation.whyCorrect: Bacterial DNA is haploid, meaning there is only one set of chromosome in the cell. This makes sense given that bacteria undergo clonal division rather than sexual reproduction, so a second parental genome is never contributed. With a single copy of each gene there is no pairing of alleles to be dominant or recessive.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Proofreading by DNA polymerase III affects error rate, not the number of gene copies in the cell.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Bacteria are prokaryotes and have no nucleus in which to package DNA.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Bacteria produce two clones of the same cell by binary fission; no second parent contributes DNA.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Bacteria both transcribe and translate their DNA, using their own 70S ribosomes.

questions.stem: Which of the following correctly describes the ribosome of a bacterial cell?

choices.label: A
choices.text: 60S, composed of a 40S large subunit and a 30S small subunit

choices.label: B
choices.text: 70S, composed of a 50S large subunit and a 30S small subunit

choices.label: C
choices.text: 70S, composed of a 60S large subunit and a 40S small subunit

choices.label: D
choices.text: 80S, composed of a 50S large subunit and a 30S small subunit

choices.label: E
choices.text: 80S, composed of a 60S large subunit and a 40S small subunit

explanation.summary: Bacterial ribosomes are 70S (50S + 30S); human ribosomes are 80S (60S + 40S).
explanation.whyCorrect: Bacterial and human ribosomes differ in size and structure. The bacterial ribosome is 70S and is built from a 50S large subunit and a 30S small subunit. That structural difference from the human 80S ribosome is what makes the bacterial ribosome a usable antibiotic target.

whyWrongByChoice.A: 60S is a eukaryotic large subunit; no ribosome has this described composition.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The 60S and 40S subunits belong to the human 80S ribosome, not to a 70S ribosome.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The 50S and 30S subunits combine to form a 70S ribosome, not an 80S ribosome.
whyWrongByChoice.E: This is the human (eukaryotic) 80S ribosome, not the bacterial one.

questions.stem: A 40-year-old man who removed an attached tick 10 days ago now has fever, headache, and a spreading rash. He is treated with doxycycline. This drug produces its antibacterial effect by binding which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Bacterial DNA polymerase III at the replication fork

choices.label: B
choices.text: Penicillin-binding proteins of the bacterial cell wall

choices.label: C
choices.text: The 30S small subunit of the bacterial ribosome

choices.label: D
choices.text: The 50S large subunit of the bacterial ribosome

choices.label: E
choices.text: The 60S large subunit of the human ribosome

explanation.summary: Tetracyclines such as doxycycline bind the 30S subunit of the bacterial ribosome and block protein production.
explanation.whyCorrect: Tetracyclines, including doxycycline, target the 30S subunit of the bacterial ribosome and thereby prevent bacterial protein production. Doxycycline is a common choice in zoonotic infections such as Lyme disease and Rocky Mountain spotted fever, which fits this tick-exposure vignette.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Doxycycline inhibits protein production and does not act on DNA replication enzymes.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Penicillin-binding proteins are the target of β-lactam antibiotics such as ampicillin.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Tetracyclines act at the 30S small subunit rather than at the 50S large subunit.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The human 80S ribosome and its 60S subunit are spared; that selectivity is why the drug is usable.

questions.stem: An antimicrobial agent inhibits protein synthesis in a Streptococcus culture but leaves cultured human cells unaffected at the same concentration. Which of the following best accounts for this selectivity?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Bacterial and human ribosomes differ in size and in structure

choices.label: B
choices.text: Bacterial cells contain a nucleus that excludes the drug

choices.label: C
choices.text: Bacterial cells lack ribosomes and import protein from the host

choices.label: D
choices.text: Human cells lack ribosomes and do not synthesize any protein

choices.label: E
choices.text: Human cells replicate their chromosomes from a single origin

explanation.summary: Antibiotics can target bacterial ribosomes because the 70S bacterial ribosome differs structurally from the human 80S ribosome.
explanation.whyCorrect: Bacterial cells carry much of the same molecular machinery as human cells, including ribosomes. Because bacterial ribosomes differ in size and structure from human ribosomes (70S with 50S and 30S subunits versus 80S with 60S and 40S subunits), they are common targets for antibiotics that spare the host.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Bacteria are prokaryotes and have no nucleus.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Bacteria carry their own 70S ribosomes and make their own protein.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Human cells have 80S ribosomes and synthesize protein continuously.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Origin number is a feature of DNA replication, and it is humans who use multiple origins.

questions.stem: A single bacterial cell contaminating a nutrient broth divides by binary fission without restriction. Approximately how many cells are present after 30 division cycles?

choices.label: A
choices.text: 1 billion cells

choices.label: B
choices.text: 1 thousand cells

choices.label: C
choices.text: 1 trillion cells

choices.label: D
choices.text: 30 cells

choices.label: E
choices.text: 60 cells

explanation.summary: Because binary fission doubles the population each cycle, 30 cycles yield roughly 1 billion cells.
explanation.whyCorrect: Bacterial cells reproduce by binary fission, producing two clones of the same cell, so the population doubles every cycle. After 30 cycles approximately 1 billion bacterial cells are present. That explosive growth is what makes colonization and invasion so easy for bacteria.

whyWrongByChoice.B: About a thousand cells is reached after roughly 10 doublings, not 30.
whyWrongByChoice.C: A trillion cells would require substantially more than 30 doublings.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Thirty is the number of division cycles; each cycle doubles the population rather than adding one cell.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Sixty would result from adding two cells per cycle, not from doubling.

questions.stem: Before a bacterium can cause infection it must first colonize, that is, establish a colony of many cells at the site. By which process do bacterial cells increase their numbers to accomplish this?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Binary fission, generating two clones of the parent cell

choices.label: B
choices.text: Budding, generating a daughter from a parental protrusion

choices.label: C
choices.text: Conjugation, generating a hybrid cell from two parents

choices.label: D
choices.text: Meiosis, generating four genetically distinct daughter cells

choices.label: E
choices.text: Transduction, generating progeny inside a viral capsid

explanation.summary: Bacteria multiply by binary fission, which yields two clones of the dividing cell.
explanation.whyCorrect: Bacterial cells reproduce by binary fission, or dividing, which results in two clones of the same bacterial cell. Repeated fission doubles the population each cycle and rapidly builds the colony needed for colonization and invasion.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Budding describes growth of organisms such as yeast, not bacterial division.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Conjugation transfers a plasmid between two cells but does not increase cell number.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Meiosis is a eukaryotic reduction division; bacteria are haploid and divide clonally.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Transduction is DNA transfer by a bacteriophage, not a mode of bacterial replication.

questions.stem: Replication of the chromosome of Escherichia coli is compared with replication of a human chromosome. Which of the following is characteristic of the bacterial process?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Replication begins at a single origin on the chromosome

choices.label: B
choices.text: Replication begins at multiple origins along the same chromosome

choices.label: C
choices.text: Replication is completed within a nuclear compartment

choices.label: D
choices.text: Replication proceeds in only one direction from the origin

choices.label: E
choices.text: Replication yields two linear daughter chromosomes

explanation.summary: Bacterial DNA replication starts at a single origin, in contrast to the multiple origins used by humans.
explanation.whyCorrect: The circular, chromosomal, double-stranded bacterial DNA is unwound by a bacterial helicase that starts at a single origin of replication. Humans, in contrast, have multiple origins of replication on the same DNA strand. From that single bacterial origin, replication then proceeds in both directions.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Multiple origins on one strand is the human pattern, not the bacterial one.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Bacteria are prokaryotes and have no nucleus in which replication could occur.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Replication proceeds in both directions from the bacterial origin of replication.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The bacterial product is two identical circular double-stranded chromosomes.

questions.stem: The first step in replication of the circular bacterial chromosome is separation of the two parental strands at the origin. Which enzyme performs this step?

choices.label: A
choices.text: DNA polymerase III

choices.label: B
choices.text: Helicase

choices.label: C
choices.text: Reverse transcriptase

choices.label: D
choices.text: Transposase

choices.label: E
choices.text: β-lactamase

explanation.summary: A bacterial helicase unwinds the double-stranded circular chromosome at the single origin of replication.
explanation.whyCorrect: Before bacteria can divide they must replicate their DNA, and the circular double-stranded chromosome is first unwound by a bacterial helicase acting at the single origin of replication. Only after unwinding can DNA polymerase III copy the exposed strands.

whyWrongByChoice.A: DNA polymerase III synthesizes and proofreads the new strand after the DNA has been unwound.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Reverse transcriptase copies RNA into DNA and is not part of bacterial chromosome replication.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Transposase-type enzymes cleave and ligate at transposon sequences to relocate genes.
whyWrongByChoice.E: β-lactamase degrades penicillin molecules and plays no role in DNA replication.

questions.stem: After the bacterial chromosome is unwound at the origin, new DNA strands are synthesized and are simultaneously proofread. Which enzyme is chiefly responsible for this?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Bacterial helicase

choices.label: B
choices.text: DNA polymerase III

choices.label: C
choices.text: Penicillin-binding protein

choices.label: D
choices.text: Phage integrase

choices.label: E
choices.text: RNA polymerase

explanation.summary: DNA polymerase III replicates the bacterial DNA strand while proofreading the daughter strand.
explanation.whyCorrect: Once helicase has unwound the chromosome, DNA polymerase III replicates the DNA strand while simultaneously proofreading the child strand. Bacterial DNA replication is mainly mediated by this enzyme, and the result is two identical circular double-stranded chromosomes.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Helicase unwinds the double helix but does not synthesize new DNA.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Penicillin-binding proteins cross-link the peptidoglycan cell wall.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Phage integrase inserts viral DNA into the host chromosome during lysogeny.
whyWrongByChoice.E: RNA polymerase carries out transcription, producing RNA from a DNA template.

questions.stem: Replication of the Escherichia coli chromosome is simpler and quicker than replication of a human chromosome. Which of the following best explains this difference?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The bacterial genome contains about 245 million base pairs

choices.label: B
choices.text: The bacterial genome contains about 5 million base pairs

choices.label: C
choices.text: The bacterial genome is copied by host nuclear enzymes

choices.label: D
choices.text: The bacterial genome is copied only during the S phase

choices.label: E
choices.text: The bacterial genome is copied without any proofreading step

explanation.summary: The E. coli chromosome is roughly 5 million base pairs versus about 245 million in humans, so replication is shorter and faster.
explanation.whyCorrect: Bacterial DNA replication is very similar to that in humans, but bacterial DNA is much shorter, approximately 5 million base pairs in Escherichia coli compared with about 245 million in humans. Because the molecule to be copied is far smaller, the process is simpler and quicker, and E. coli can divide as often as every 20 minutes.

whyWrongByChoice.A: About 245 million base pairs is the approximate human figure, not the bacterial one.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Bacteria use their own replication enzymes and have no nucleus.
whyWrongByChoice.D: S phase is a eukaryotic cell-cycle concept; bacteria replicate as they divide clonally.
whyWrongByChoice.E: DNA polymerase III does proofread the daughter strand while replicating it.

questions.stem: A bacterium completes one round of chromosomal DNA replication. Which of the following best describes the product?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Four identical circular single-stranded chromosomes

choices.label: B
choices.text: One circular chromosome and one linear chromosome

choices.label: C
choices.text: One circular chromosome with a single-stranded gap

choices.label: D
choices.text: Two identical circular double-stranded chromosomes

choices.label: E
choices.text: Two identical linear double-stranded chromosomes

explanation.summary: Bacterial chromosome replication produces two identical circular, double-stranded DNA chromosomes.
explanation.whyCorrect: The circular double-stranded bacterial chromosome is unwound by helicase and copied by DNA polymerase III, and the result is two identical, circular, double-stranded DNA chromosomes. One goes to each daughter cell when the bacterium divides by binary fission.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Replication doubles the chromosome once, and the products are double-stranded.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Both products are circular; replication does not generate a linear chromosome.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Both strands are completed, so no single-stranded gap remains at the end of replication.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Because the parental chromosome is circular, the daughter molecules are circular as well.

questions.stem: Escherichia coli is known to divide as often as every 20 minutes, and bacteria possess only minimal DNA repair mechanisms. Which of the following is the expected consequence for the bacterial population?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Accumulation of spontaneous mutations in the genome

choices.label: B
choices.text: Arrest of division until repair enzymes are induced

choices.label: C
choices.text: Complete genetic uniformity across all of the progeny

choices.label: D
choices.text: Conversion of the chromosome from circular to linear

choices.label: E
choices.text: Progressive loss of the plasmid content of the cells

explanation.summary: Rapid division plus minimal repair produces spontaneous mutations, some of which are advantageous to the bacteria.
explanation.whyCorrect: A simpler genome and a very rapid division rate leave a great deal of room for errors during DNA replication, and errors in DNA sequence give rise to spontaneous mutations. The combination of minimal repair mechanisms and speed of cell division is what drives bacterial evolution. Not all of these mutations are bad for bacteria, since some confer rewards such as antibiotic resistance.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Bacteria continue to divide rapidly; the errors are simply carried forward to progeny.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Replication errors make the progeny genetically variable despite clonal division.
