whyWrongByChoice.B: Increased peristalsis is not the described mechanism by which flora maintain the barrier.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Lactic acid acidification of a mucosal surface is the vaginal mechanism, not the colonic barrier effect.
whyWrongByChoice.D: A polysaccharide capsule is a bacterial virulence factor promoting invasion, not a host barrier.

questions.topicName: Normal Flora: Role in Health and Disease

questions.stem: A hospital infection control team reviews carriage of Staphylococcus aureus among healthy adults. Approximately what proportion of people carry S. aureus as part of their normal flora?

choices.label: A
choices.text: About 5%

choices.label: B
choices.text: About 10%

choices.label: C
choices.text: About 20%

choices.label: D
choices.text: About 30%

choices.label: E
choices.text: About 60%

explanation.summary: About 30% of people carry S. aureus as normal flora, and an additional 30 to 50% carry it transiently.
explanation.whyCorrect: S. aureus can be found in the nasal passages, on the skin, and in the pharynx, gastrointestinal tract, and vagina. Roughly 30% of people carry it as established normal flora, while 30 to 50% carry it transiently, meaning colonization comes and goes and may involve one site such as the nares but not others.

whyWrongByChoice.A: This markedly underestimates the proportion of the population colonized by S. aureus.
whyWrongByChoice.B: This underestimates S. aureus carriage among healthy people.
whyWrongByChoice.C: This is below the proportion described for persistent S. aureus carriage.
whyWrongByChoice.E: This overstates persistent carriage, which is closer to the transient carriage range.

questions.topicName: Normal Flora: Role in Health and Disease

questions.stem: A sexually active 20-year-old woman has dysuria and urinary frequency. Urine culture grows an organism that is normal flora of the gastrointestinal tract and vagina and is the second most common cause of urinary tract infection. Which of the following is the most likely organism?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Enterococcus species

choices.label: B
choices.text: Escherichia coli

choices.label: C
choices.text: Gardnerella vaginalis

choices.label: D
choices.text: Lactobacillus species

choices.label: E
choices.text: Staphylococcus saprophyticus

explanation.summary: S. saprophyticus is normal flora of the GI tract and vagina and is the second most common cause of urinary tract infection after E. coli.
explanation.whyCorrect: Staphylococcus species are normal flora that commonly cause community and hospital infections. S. saprophyticus colonizes the gastrointestinal tract and vagina, and only E. coli, itself normal flora of the GI tract, causes more urinary tract infections than S. saprophyticus does.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Enterococcus is colonic and vaginal flora but is not the organism described as second most common.
whyWrongByChoice.B: E. coli is the single most common cause of urinary tract infection, not the second most common.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Gardnerella overgrowth causes bacterial vaginosis rather than urinary tract infection.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Lactobacillus is the protective dominant vaginal flora and is not a common urinary pathogen.

questions.topicName: Normal Flora: Role in Health and Disease

questions.stem: A dermatology resident swabs intact skin from a healthy volunteer and cultures the sample. Which of the following groups of organisms is most characteristic of normal skin flora?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Bacteroides, Bifidobacterium, and Enterococcus species

choices.label: B
choices.text: Lactobacillus, Gardnerella, and Candida species

choices.label: C
choices.text: S. epidermidis, Cutibacterium acnes, and Malassezia species

choices.label: D
choices.text: S. pneumoniae, H. influenzae, and M. catarrhalis

choices.label: E
choices.text: Veillonella, Prevotella, and Fusobacterium species

explanation.summary: Skin normal flora includes Staphylococcus epidermidis, Cutibacterium (formerly Propionibacterium) acnes, Corynebacterium and Micrococcus species, and the fungus Malassezia.
explanation.whyCorrect: The skin carries roughly 10^11 microbes. Its characteristic residents are S. epidermidis, Propionibacterium acnes (now called Cutibacterium acnes), Corynebacterium species, Micrococcus species, the fungus Malassezia, and occasionally S. aureus.

whyWrongByChoice.A: These organisms are members of the colonic and small-bowel flora.
whyWrongByChoice.B: These organisms characterize the vaginal tract rather than the skin surface.
whyWrongByChoice.D: These organisms are nasopharyngeal flora associated with acute otitis media.
whyWrongByChoice.E: These anaerobes are typical of dental plaque and saliva rather than skin.

questions.topicName: Normal Flora: Role in Health and Disease

questions.stem: A student compares the microbial density of different body sites. Which of the following sites harbors approximately 10^12 microbes, a number second only to the colon?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Dental plaque

choices.label: B
choices.text: Ileum

choices.label: C
choices.text: Saliva

choices.label: D
choices.text: Skin

choices.label: E
choices.text: Vagina

explanation.summary: Dental plaque carries about 10^12 microbes, more than any site except the colon.
explanation.whyCorrect: Estimated microbial numbers by site place the colon highest at about 10^14, followed by dental plaque at about 10^12. Plaque is densely colonized by Streptococcus species such as S. mutans along with Actinomyces, Veillonella, Fusobacterium, and Prevotella species.

whyWrongByChoice.B: The ileum carries about 10^11 microbes.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Saliva carries about 10^11 microbes, an order of magnitude below dental plaque.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Skin carries about 10^11 microbes.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The vagina carries about 10^7 to 10^8 microbes, among the lower counts listed.

questions.topicName: Normal Flora: Role in Health and Disease

questions.stem: A microbiology instructor asks a class to identify an example of dysbiosis. Which of the following best fits that definition?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Acquisition of maternal flora during vaginal delivery

choices.label: B
choices.text: Any colonization of the skin by Staphylococcus aureus

choices.label: C
choices.text: Presence of normal flora in a site that should be sterile

choices.label: D
choices.text: Production of lactic acid by vaginal Lactobacillus species

choices.label: E
choices.text: Transient carriage of a microbe that later disappears

explanation.summary: Dysbiosis is an unhealthy change in the microbiota: overgrowth of normal flora, inadequate growth of normal flora, or microbes in a site that should be sterile.
explanation.whyCorrect: Unhealthy changes in the microbiota are termed dysbiosis, and the definition includes three situations: overgrowth of the normal flora, inadequate growth of the normal flora, and the presence of microbes in a site that should be sterile. Spillage of colonic flora into the peritoneal cavity is a classic example of the third.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Acquiring maternal flora at birth is normal establishment of the microbiota.
whyWrongByChoice.B: About 30% of healthy people carry S. aureus as normal flora, so colonization alone is not dysbiosis.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Lactic acid production by Lactobacillus is a healthy protective function of the vaginal flora.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Transient carriage is a normal pattern of colonization, seen with S. aureus in 30 to 50% of people.

questions.topicName: Normal Flora: Role in Health and Disease

questions.stem: A gastroenterologist describes the microbial population of the healthy adult colon to a group of students. Which of the following best characterizes it?

choices.label: A
choices.text: About 10^11 microbes, predominantly aerobic Micrococcus species

choices.label: B
choices.text: About 10^12 microbes, predominantly aerobic Streptococcus species

choices.label: C
choices.text: About 10^14 microbes, predominantly anaerobic Bacteroides species

choices.label: D
choices.text: About 10^7 microbes, predominantly aerobic Lactobacillus species

choices.label: E
choices.text: About 10^8 microbes, predominantly anaerobic Gardnerella species

explanation.summary: The colon holds roughly 10^14 microbes that are mostly anaerobes, with Bacteroides species prominent among them.
explanation.whyCorrect: The large intestine is the most densely colonized site in the body, carrying about 10^14 organisms. These are mostly anaerobes, including Bacteroides species, Firmicutes such as Clostridium and Lactobacillus, Actinobacteria such as Bifidobacterium, Proteobacteria such as Escherichia coli, and Enterococcus species.

whyWrongByChoice.A: About 10^11 corresponds to sites such as skin, saliva, and ileum, and Micrococcus is a skin organism.
whyWrongByChoice.B: About 10^12 corresponds to dental plaque, where Streptococcus species predominate.
whyWrongByChoice.D: About 10^7 microbes corresponds to the stomach, duodenum, and jejunum rather than the colon.
whyWrongByChoice.E: About 10^8 corresponds to the vagina, where Gardnerella may be found in some women.

questions.topicName: Normal Flora: Role in Health and Disease

questions.stem: A physician tells a patient that the organism causing her infection is an opportunistic pathogen. Which of the following best defines that term?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A microbe acquired only from the hospital environment

choices.label: B
choices.text: A microbe that always causes disease when it is acquired

choices.label: C
choices.text: A microbe that causes disease only under certain conditions

choices.label: D
choices.text: A microbe that is transmitted exclusively by sexual contact

choices.label: E
choices.text: A microbe that lives on a host without benefit or harm

explanation.summary: Opportunistic pathogens do not usually cause infection in healthy individuals but can do so under certain conditions.
explanation.whyCorrect: Most members of the normal flora are harmless, but some are opportunistic pathogens: microbes that do not usually cause infection in healthy people but can when conditions permit. Common permissive conditions include disruption of the normal flora, immunosuppression, trauma, comorbidities, and dietary issues.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Opportunists such as Candida albicans are members of a person's own normal flora, not hospital-only organisms.
whyWrongByChoice.B: An organism that always causes disease on acquisition is a frank pathogen, not an opportunist.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Opportunistic infections such as thrush and pseudomembranous colitis are not sexually transmitted.
whyWrongByChoice.E: A microbe living on the host without benefit or harm is a commensal.

questions.topicName: Normal Flora: Role in Health and Disease

questions.stem: A laboratory technician performs a Gram stain on a wound swab. After crystal violet is applied and fixed with iodine, the slide is decolorized with acetone and then counterstained. One population of organisms remains deep purple under the microscope. Which feature of these organisms best explains the retained purple color?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A polysaccharide capsule that preferentially binds safranin

choices.label: B
choices.text: A thick cell wall that holds the crystal violet dye

choices.label: C
choices.text: A thin cell wall that releases dye during decolorization

choices.label: D
choices.text: A waxy surface coat that repels all aqueous dyes

choices.label: E
choices.text: An outer membrane that excludes the crystal violet dye

explanation.summary: Gram-positive bacteria keep crystal violet because their cell walls are thick.
explanation.whyCorrect: In the Gram stain, bacteria are stained with crystal violet, fixed with iodine, and then decolorized with alcohol or acetone. Gram-positive bacteria retain the purple dye because of their thick cell walls, so they appear purple at the end of the procedure. Gram-negative organisms, whose cell walls are thinner, lose the dye during decolorization.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Safranin is the counterstain that colors decolorized organisms red; it does not account for a purple result.
whyWrongByChoice.C: A thin cell wall is exactly what allows the dye to wash out, producing a gram-negative result.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Organisms with a waxy surface are the ones that cannot be stained reliably by Gram stain at all, which is why other stains are needed for them.
whyWrongByChoice.E: An outer membrane is a gram-negative feature, and those organisms lose the crystal violet rather than retaining it.

questions.stem: During the same Gram stain, a second organism on the slide loses the crystal violet after the alcohol wash and appears red when the procedure is complete. Which dye accounts for the red color of this organism?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Crystal violet

choices.label: B
choices.text: Eosin Y

choices.label: C
choices.text: Methylene blue

choices.label: D
choices.text: Neutral red

choices.label: E
choices.text: Safranin

explanation.summary: Safranin is the counterstain that makes gram-negative bacteria red.
explanation.whyCorrect: Gram-negative bacteria have thinner cell walls and lose crystal violet during decolorization. They are then counterstained red with safranin, which is what allows them to be seen and classified as gram negative.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Crystal violet is the primary purple dye, and it has already been washed out of this organism.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Eosin Y is also an EMB agar ingredient used to inhibit gram-positive growth and color colonies on a plate.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Methylene blue is an ingredient of eosin methylene blue agar, not the Gram stain counterstain.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Neutral red is the pH indicator in MacConkey agar, where it colors lactose-fermenting colonies.

questions.stem: A 6-year-old unimmunized child has a sore throat and a gray membrane over the tonsils. Gram stain of a throat swab shows gram-positive rods that are wider at one end, giving them a club shape. Which organism shows this characteristic morphology?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Bacillus spp.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Corynebacterium spp.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Fusobacterium spp.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Salmonella spp.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Vibrio spp.

explanation.summary: Club-shaped rods are the classic morphology of Corynebacterium diphtheriae.
explanation.whyCorrect: Shape and arrangement are recorded during the Gram stain because they narrow the differential immediately. Among the common morphologies, the club-shaped rod is the pattern assigned to Corynebacterium diphtheriae.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Bacillus spp. are rods with square ends, not rods that flare at one end.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Fusobacterium spp. are fusiform, tapering at both ends rather than clubbing at one.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Salmonella spp. are rods with rounded ends and are gram negative besides.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Vibrio spp. are curved, comma-shaped gram-negative organisms.

questions.stem: A 19-year-old college student has fever, headache, and neck stiffness. Gram stain of cerebrospinal fluid shows gram-negative cocci in pairs, each cell flattened along the side it shares with its partner, giving a kidney-bean appearance. Which genus shows this pattern?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Bacillus

choices.label: B
choices.text: Borrelia

choices.label: C
choices.text: Neisseria

choices.label: D
choices.text: Staphylococcus

choices.label: E
choices.text: Streptococcus

explanation.summary: Kidney-bean-shaped cocci in pairs are Neisseria spp.
explanation.whyCorrect: Bacteria that form pairs are described as diplococci, and Neisseria spp. are the classic example. Their paired cells have a kidney bean shape, which together with the gram-negative staining identifies the genus.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Bacillus spp. are gram-positive rods with square ends, not cocci.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Borrelia spp. are spirochetes with a relaxed coil, not cocci.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Staphylococcus spp. form grape-like clusters and are gram positive.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Streptococcus spp. form chains of cocci and are gram positive.

questions.stem: A 68-year-old man with lobar pneumonia has a sputum Gram stain showing gram-positive cocci in pairs, with the outer end of each cell tapered to a point. Which organism is most consistent with this morphology?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Enterococcus faecalis

choices.label: B
choices.text: Neisseria meningitidis

choices.label: C
choices.text: Staphylococcus aureus

choices.label: D
choices.text: Streptococcus pneumoniae

choices.label: E
choices.text: Streptococcus pyogenes

explanation.summary: Cocci in pairs with pointed ends are Streptococcus pneumoniae.
explanation.whyCorrect: Most streptococci grow in chains, but Streptococcus pneumoniae is distinguished by growing in pairs whose outer ends are pointed. That morphology, in a gram-positive organism from sputum, points directly to S. pneumoniae.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Enterococcus faecalis is a gram-positive coccus that grows in chains rather than pointed pairs.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Neisseria meningitidis is a gram-negative diplococcus with kidney-bean-shaped cells.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Staphylococcus aureus grows in grape-like clusters, not in pairs with tapered ends.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Streptococcus pyogenes grows in chains, the general streptococcal pattern.

questions.stem: A preparation from a genital ulcer shows slender spiral organisms whose coils are wound tightly and regularly, like the threads on a screw. Based on the coiling pattern, which genus is favored?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Borrelia

choices.label: B
choices.text: Fusobacterium

choices.label: C
choices.text: Spirillum

choices.label: D
choices.text: Treponema

choices.label: E
choices.text: Vibrio

explanation.summary: Tightly coiled spirochetes are Treponema; relaxed coils are Borrelia.
explanation.whyCorrect: Spirochetes have a twisted shape like the threads on a screw, and the tightness of the coil separates the genera. Tightly coiled spirochetes correspond to Treponema spp., which is what this preparation shows.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Borrelia spp. are the spirochetes described as having a relaxed coil, not a tight one.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Fusobacterium spp. are fusiform rods that taper at each end and are not spiral.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Spirillum organisms have a wavy shape, which is not the tight screw-thread coil described.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Vibrio spp. are curved, comma-shaped organisms rather than spirals.

questions.stem: A Gram stain of pus from a skin abscess shows gram-positive cocci bunched together in irregular, grape-like groups. Which genus has this arrangement?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Clostridium

choices.label: B
choices.text: Corynebacterium

choices.label: C
choices.text: Neisseria

choices.label: D
choices.text: Staphylococcus

choices.label: E
choices.text: Streptococcus

explanation.summary: Gram-positive cocci in grape-like clusters are staphylococci.
explanation.whyCorrect: Grouping patterns are recorded alongside shape. Clusters, in which the bacteria bunch together like grapes, are the arrangement of Staphylococcus spp., and all Staphylococcus spp. are gram-positive cocci in clusters.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Clostridium organisms are gram-positive rods that grow only without oxygen.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Corynebacterium organisms are club-shaped rods, not cocci.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Neisseria spp. are gram-negative organisms that form pairs, not clusters.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Streptococcus spp. form short single-file chains rather than clusters.

questions.stem: A woman with vulvovaginal itching and thick white discharge has a swab sent for culture, and the laboratory needs to recover the suspected yeast from a site that carries heavy normal bacterial flora. Which medium is designed for this purpose?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Eosin methylene blue agar

choices.label: B
choices.text: MacConkey agar

choices.label: C
choices.text: Mannitol salt agar

choices.label: D
choices.text: Sabouraud dextrose agar

choices.label: E
choices.text: Thayer-Martin agar

explanation.summary: Sabouraud dextrose agar is the selective medium for fungi.
explanation.whyCorrect: Sabouraud dextrose agar has an acidic pH and contains antibiotics that inhibit bacterial growth, so it is selective for fungi such as Candida spp. and Aspergillus spp. Candidiasis occurs at sites loaded with normal flora, which is exactly when a selective fungal medium is needed.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Eosin methylene blue agar is used for gram-negative bacteria and their lactose fermentation.
whyWrongByChoice.B: MacConkey agar is aimed at gram-negative bacteria through bile salts and crystal violet.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Mannitol salt agar uses high salt to select staphylococci, not yeast.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Thayer-Martin agar contains nystatin to inhibit fungi, so it would suppress the organism being sought.

questions.stem: Thayer-Martin medium is inoculated with a specimen to recover Neisseria gonorrhoeae. Which component of this medium suppresses the gram-positive bacteria present in the specimen?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Bile salts

choices.label: B
choices.text: Colistin

choices.label: C
choices.text: Nystatin

choices.label: D
choices.text: Trimethoprim

choices.label: E
choices.text: Vancomycin

explanation.summary: Vancomycin is the Thayer-Martin ingredient that inhibits gram-positive bacteria.
explanation.whyCorrect: Thayer-Martin agar contains antibiotics that inhibit most bacteria and fungi so that Neisseria can be isolated. Within that mixture, vancomycin is the agent directed at gram-positive bacteria.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Bile salts are a MacConkey agar ingredient and are not part of Thayer-Martin medium.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Colistin inhibits most gram-negative bacteria other than the Neisseria being selected.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Nystatin is included in Thayer-Martin agar to inhibit fungi, not gram-positive bacteria.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Trimethoprim likewise acts against most gram-negative bacteria in the specimen.

questions.stem: A rectal swab from a man being screened for gonorrhea is plated on both chocolate agar and Thayer-Martin agar. The chocolate plate is overgrown with mixed colonies, while the Thayer-Martin plate yields only a few distinct colonies. Which statement best explains this difference?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Chocolate agar changes color when the normal flora ferment lactose.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Chocolate agar lacks the nutrients that Neisseria requires for growth.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Thayer-Martin agar contains antibiotics that suppress the normal flora.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Thayer-Martin agar forms a black precipitate with the normal flora.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Thayer-Martin agar lyses the organisms that are soluble in bile salts.

explanation.summary: Selective media are used at sites rich in normal flora so the pathogen is not overgrown.
explanation.whyCorrect: The rectum carries heavy normal flora. On a non-selective agar such as chocolate agar, that flora overwhelms the plate and makes N. gonorrhoeae very difficult to isolate. Thayer-Martin agar contains antibiotics that suppress the competing organisms, leaving Neisseria to grow.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Chocolate agar is not a lactose-based differential medium, so no fermentation color change occurs.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Chocolate agar supports Neisseria growth well; the problem is overgrowth by other organisms, not a lack of nutrients.
whyWrongByChoice.D: A black precipitate signals hydrogen sulfide production on triple sugar iron agar, not growth on Thayer-Martin agar.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Bile solubility is a separate assay used with the alpha-hemolytic streptococci, not a property of Thayer-Martin agar.

questions.stem: Colonies growing on blood agar are surrounded by a greenish-brown zone of discoloration, but the agar around them is not cleared. Which description of this result is correct?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Alpha hemolysis, from partial oxidation of hemoglobin

choices.label: B
choices.text: Beta hemolysis, from complete lysis of red blood cells

choices.label: C
choices.text: Beta hemolysis, from partial oxidation of hemoglobin

choices.label: D
choices.text: Gamma hemolysis, from an absence of red cell lysis

choices.label: E
choices.text: Gamma hemolysis, from complete lysis of red blood cells

explanation.summary: Greenish discoloration without clearing is alpha hemolysis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Blood agar contains sheep's blood and is used to read hemolytic patterns. Alpha hemolysis is partial oxidation of hemoglobin, which produces a greenish or brown discoloration around the colonies without clearing the agar.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Beta hemolysis is complete hemolysis and produces a clear zone, which is not present here.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Beta hemolysis is complete lysis, not partial oxidation of hemoglobin.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Gamma hemolysis means no hemolysis and no change in the agar, but this plate shows discoloration.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Gamma hemolysis specifically involves no lysis of red blood cells at all.

questions.stem: A throat culture from a child with pharyngitis grows colonies on blood agar that are surrounded by a completely clear, transparent zone. Which organism is most consistent with this finding?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Enterococcus faecalis

choices.label: B
choices.text: Streptococcus mitis

choices.label: C
choices.text: Streptococcus mutans

choices.label: D
choices.text: Streptococcus pneumoniae

choices.label: E
choices.text: Streptococcus pyogenes

explanation.summary: A clear zone on blood agar is beta hemolysis, seen with Streptococcus pyogenes.
explanation.whyCorrect: Beta hemolysis is complete hemolysis, producing a clear zone around the colonies. Streptococcus pyogenes is the beta-hemolytic streptococcus typically recovered from pharyngitis.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Enterococcus faecalis shows gamma hemolysis with no change in the agar.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Streptococcus mitis is also a viridans group organism with an alpha-hemolytic pattern.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Streptococcus mutans belongs to the viridans group and is alpha hemolytic.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Streptococcus pneumoniae is alpha hemolytic, giving greenish discoloration rather than clearing.

questions.stem: Blood agar inoculated with a gram-positive coccus shows growth with no change in the surrounding agar, with neither clearing nor discoloration. Which organism is most consistent with this result?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Enterococcus faecalis

choices.label: B
choices.text: Streptococcus agalactiae

choices.label: C
choices.text: Streptococcus mitis

choices.label: D
choices.text: Streptococcus pneumoniae

choices.label: E
choices.text: Streptococcus pyogenes

explanation.summary: No hemolysis and no agar change is gamma hemolysis, typified by Enterococcus faecalis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Gamma hemolysis means the organism does not lyse red blood cells, so the agar is unchanged. Enterococcus faecalis is the example given for this pattern.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Streptococcus agalactiae is also beta hemolytic and clears the agar.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Streptococcus mitis is a viridans organism with alpha hemolysis.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Streptococcus pneumoniae is alpha hemolytic, producing greenish discoloration.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Streptococcus pyogenes produces beta hemolysis with a clear zone around colonies.

questions.stem: A gram-negative bacillus is inoculated into a triple sugar iron slant. After incubation, the butt of the tube is black. Which reaction produced this color?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Fermentation of lactose, which acidifies the medium

choices.label: B
choices.text: Hydrolysis of urea, which alkalinizes the medium

choices.label: C
choices.text: Oxidation of cytochrome c, which darkens the reagent

choices.label: D
choices.text: Production of H2S, which precipitates as ferrous sulfide

choices.label: E
choices.text: Release of gas, which cracks and displaces the medium

explanation.summary: Black color in TSI agar means hydrogen sulfide production.
explanation.whyCorrect: TSI agar contains sodium thiosulfate and ferrous sulfate. When an organism produces H2S, the gas reacts with the iron to form ferrous sulfide, an insoluble black precipitate. Because H2S formation requires an acidic environment, a black tube also implies acid conditions.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Fermentation produces acid, which turns the agar yellow rather than black.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Urea hydrolysis is read in a separate urea broth, where phenol red turns pink.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The oxidase assay is performed on filter paper and gives a blue or dark purple reagent, not a black agar butt.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Gas production shows up as bubbles or cracks in the agar, with no color change.

questions.stem: A triple sugar iron slant inoculated with an enteric isolate turns yellow after incubation. Which bacterial activity does this color change indicate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Breakdown of hydrogen peroxide, with oxygen production

choices.label: B
choices.text: Conversion of fibrinogen, with fibrin production

choices.label: C
choices.text: Fermentation of carbohydrate, with acid production

choices.label: D
choices.text: Hydrolysis of urea, with ammonia production

choices.label: E
choices.text: Reduction of thiosulfate, with sulfide production

explanation.summary: Yellow on TSI agar indicates sugar fermentation with acid production.
explanation.whyCorrect: TSI agar identifies bacteria by their ability to ferment glucose, lactose, and sucrose. Fermentation produces acid, and the acid changes the color of the agar to yellow.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Breakdown of hydrogen peroxide is the catalase reaction, read as bubbling on a slide.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Conversion of fibrinogen to fibrin is the coagulase test, read as clot formation in serum.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Urease activity generates ammonia, which is alkaline and would turn a phenol red urea broth pink.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Sulfide production forms a black precipitate in TSI agar, not a yellow color.

questions.stem: Triple sugar iron agar contains glucose at 0.1% but lactose and sucrose at 1% each. Which advantage does the low glucose concentration provide?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Glucose is kept low, so gram-positive organisms are inhibited on the slant of the tube

choices.label: B
choices.text: Glucose is kept low, so hydrogen sulfide can form without any acidic environment present

choices.label: C
choices.text: Glucose is kept low, so the pH indicator is not consumed as a nutrient by the organism

choices.label: D
choices.text: Glucose runs out early, so fermenting only glucose looks different from fermenting the disaccharides

choices.label: E
choices.text: Glucose runs out early, so gas production is prevented in the butt of the tube medium

explanation.summary: The low glucose concentration in TSI lets glucose-only fermentation be separated from lactose or sucrose fermentation.
explanation.whyCorrect: TSI agar holds three sugars: glucose at 0.1%, lactose at 1%, and sucrose at 1%. The low glucose concentration allows detection of glucose fermentation alone versus lactose or sucrose fermentation, which is what produces the differing color changes in the slant and the butt of the medium.

whyWrongByChoice.A: TSI agar is a differential medium and does not select against gram-positive organisms.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Formation of H2S actually requires an acidic environment; black color is taken as evidence that acid conditions are present.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The indicator reports pH changes and is not depleted as a nutrient by the organism.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Gas production is a separate readout of the medium, shown by bubbles or cracks, and is not suppressed by the sugar ratio.

questions.stem: A plate of mannitol salt agar is inoculated with a mixed skin swab, and only staphylococci grow. Which property of the medium accounts for the inhibition of the other organisms?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A 7.5% sodium chloride concentration

choices.label: B
choices.text: An acidic pH with added antibiotics

choices.label: C
choices.text: Bile salts with crystal violet

choices.label: D
choices.text: Eosin Y with methylene blue

choices.label: E
choices.text: Vancomycin with colistin and nystatin

explanation.summary: Mannitol salt agar is selective because of its high salt concentration.
explanation.whyCorrect: Mannitol salt agar contains 7.5% sodium chloride, a salt level that inhibits most bacteria but not the staphylococci. Staphylococci tolerate it because they normally live on skin, which also has a high salt content.

whyWrongByChoice.B: An acidic pH with antibiotics describes Sabouraud dextrose agar, which selects for fungi.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Bile salts and crystal violet are the selective agents in MacConkey agar, which targets gram-negative bacteria.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Eosin Y and methylene blue are the selective agents in EMB agar.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Vancomycin, colistin, and nystatin are the Thayer-Martin antibiotics used to select Neisseria.

questions.stem: Two staphylococcal isolates are streaked onto mannitol salt agar. One produces yellow colonies with yellow surrounding medium, and the other produces pink colonies on unchanged medium. Which organism produced the yellow colonies?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Enterococcus faecalis

choices.label: B
choices.text: Staphylococcus aureus

choices.label: C
choices.text: Staphylococcus epidermidis

choices.label: D
choices.text: Staphylococcus saprophyticus

choices.label: E
choices.text: Streptococcus pyogenes

explanation.summary: Yellow colonies on mannitol salt agar mark the mannitol fermenter, Staphylococcus aureus.
explanation.whyCorrect: Mannitol salt agar is differential because it contains mannitol and the pH indicator phenol red. Staphylococcus aureus ferments mannitol, and the acid produced turns phenol red to yellow. Other staphylococci do not ferment mannitol and give pink colonies.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Enterococcus faecalis is not a staphylococcus and is not what mannitol salt agar is designed to recover here.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Staphylococcus epidermidis does not ferment mannitol, so its colonies stay pink.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Staphylococcus saprophyticus also fails to ferment mannitol and gives pink colonies.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Streptococcus pyogenes is inhibited by the high salt concentration of the medium.

questions.stem: MacConkey agar is chosen to isolate enteric gram-negative rods from a stool specimen. Which ingredients make this medium selective for gram-negative bacteria?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Bile salts and crystal violet

choices.label: B
choices.text: Colistin and trimethoprim

choices.label: C
choices.text: Eosin Y and methylene blue

choices.label: D
choices.text: Mannitol and phenol red

choices.label: E
choices.text: Sodium thiosulfate and ferrous sulfate

explanation.summary: MacConkey agar selects for gram-negative bacteria with bile salts and crystal violet.
explanation.whyCorrect: MacConkey agar contains bile salts and crystal violet, which inhibit the growth of gram-positive bacteria. That leaves gram-negative organisms to grow, which is what makes it useful for stool and other enteric specimens.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Colistin and trimethoprim are Thayer-Martin antibiotics that inhibit most gram-negative bacteria.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Eosin Y and methylene blue are the selective agents of EMB agar, a different medium.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Mannitol and phenol red are the differential components of mannitol salt agar.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Sodium thiosulfate and ferrous sulfate are TSI agar ingredients used to detect H2S.

questions.stem: A stool isolate grown on MacConkey agar forms colorless colonies, while a control organism on the same plate forms bright pink colonies. Which conclusion about the colorless isolate is best supported?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It does not ferment lactose

choices.label: B
choices.text: It is a gram-positive organism

choices.label: C
choices.text: It produces cytochrome c oxidase

choices.label: D
choices.text: It produces hydrogen sulfide

choices.label: E
choices.text: It produces urease

explanation.summary: Colorless colonies on MacConkey agar identify a non-lactose fermenter.
explanation.whyCorrect: MacConkey agar is differential because it contains lactose and the pH indicator neutral red. Lactose-fermenting bacteria acidify the medium and produce pink or red colonies, while non-fermenters remain colorless.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Gram-positive organisms are inhibited by MacConkey agar, so a growing colony is gram negative.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Oxidase activity is detected with oxidase reagent on filter paper, which turns blue or dark purple.
whyWrongByChoice.D: H2S production is read as a black precipitate on TSI agar, not as colony color on MacConkey agar.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Urease activity is detected in urea broth, where phenol red turns pink.

questions.stem: A urine isolate plated on eosin methylene blue agar produces colonies with a distinctive bright green metallic sheen. Which organism is most likely?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Escherichia coli

choices.label: B
choices.text: Klebsiella pneumoniae

choices.label: C
choices.text: Pseudomonas aeruginosa

choices.label: D
choices.text: Salmonella spp.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Shigella spp.

explanation.summary: A green metallic sheen on EMB agar is the signature of Escherichia coli.
explanation.whyCorrect: On EMB agar, lactose fermentation normally stains colonies purple or black. E. coli is the unique exception: its rapid fermentation of lactose causes amine bonding to the dye, turning the colonies a bright metallic green.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Klebsiella pneumoniae ferments lactose but does not produce the metallic green sheen.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Pseudomonas aeruginosa does not ferment lactose, so it produces no fermentation color.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Salmonella spp. are non-lactose fermenters and are identified instead by H2S production.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Shigella spp. are also non-lactose fermenters and produce no H2S on TSI agar.

questions.stem: A gram-positive coccus is mixed with a drop of hydrogen peroxide on a slide and immediately produces vigorous bubbling. Which conclusion follows?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It is a Staphylococcus sp.; the bubbling shows catalase activity

choices.label: B
choices.text: It is a Staphylococcus sp.; the bubbling shows coagulase activity

choices.label: C
choices.text: It is a Streptococcus sp.; the bubbling shows catalase activity

choices.label: D
choices.text: It is a Streptococcus sp.; the bubbling shows coagulase activity

choices.label: E
choices.text: It is an Enterococcus sp.; the bubbling shows urease activity

explanation.summary: Bubbling with hydrogen peroxide is a positive catalase test, which separates staphylococci from streptococci.
explanation.whyCorrect: Catalase breaks hydrogen peroxide down into water and oxygen, and the released oxygen appears as bubbles. All Staphylococcus spp. are catalase positive and all Streptococcus spp. are catalase negative, so a bubbling gram-positive coccus is a staphylococcus.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Coagulase activity is not what hydrogen peroxide detects; the bubbling reflects catalase.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Streptococcus spp. are catalase negative, so they would not bubble in hydrogen peroxide.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Coagulase is tested with serum and read as clot formation, and streptococci are catalase negative regardless.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Urease is tested in urea broth by a color change, and enterococci are catalase negative.

questions.stem: Catalase-producing bacteria rapidly break down hydrogen peroxide. Which consequence of this enzyme activity most directly helps the organism survive within a host?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It allows growth in media containing 7.5% sodium chloride

choices.label: B
choices.text: It converts host fibrinogen into a protective fibrin clot

choices.label: C
choices.text: It hydrolyzes host urea to neutralize surrounding acid

choices.label: D
choices.text: It lyses host red blood cells to release usable nutrients

choices.label: E
choices.text: It reduces the reactive oxygen species used in phagocytic killing

explanation.summary: Catalase degrades hydrogen peroxide, making bacteria resistant to phagocytic killing.
explanation.whyCorrect: Some microbes produce catalase to reduce the accumulation of reactive oxygen species derived from hydrogen peroxide. Because phagocytes use those reactive species to kill ingested bacteria, catalase production makes the organism resistant to phagocytic killing.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Salt tolerance is a separate property, exploited by mannitol salt agar rather than by catalase.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Converting fibrinogen to fibrin is the activity of coagulase, which is a different enzyme.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Hydrolyzing urea to ammonia and carbon dioxide is the activity of urease.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Lysing red blood cells is hemolysis, read on blood agar and unrelated to catalase.

questions.stem: A catalase-positive, gram-positive coccus growing in clusters is mixed with serum, and a visible clot forms. Which organism is identified, and by which enzyme activity?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Staphylococcus aureus, by catalase acting on fibrinogen

choices.label: B
choices.text: Staphylococcus aureus, by coagulase acting on fibrinogen

choices.label: C
choices.text: Staphylococcus epidermidis, by catalase acting on peroxide

choices.label: D
choices.text: Staphylococcus saprophyticus, by urease acting on urea

choices.label: E
choices.text: Streptococcus pyogenes, by coagulase acting on fibrinogen

explanation.summary: Among the staphylococci, only S. aureus is coagulase positive.
explanation.whyCorrect: The coagulase test distinguishes S. aureus from the other staphylococci. Coagulase catalyzes the conversion of fibrinogen to fibrin, so when the bacteria are mixed with serum, which contains fibrinogen, a clot forms only if the organism produces coagulase.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Catalase acts on hydrogen peroxide, not on fibrinogen, so it cannot produce a clot.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Staphylococcus epidermidis is coagulase negative and would leave the serum unclotted.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Staphylococcus saprophyticus is also coagulase negative, and urease is not what the serum test detects.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Streptococcus pyogenes is catalase negative, which the stem has already excluded.

questions.stem: A sexually active 21-year-old woman has dysuria, and urine culture grows a coagulase-negative, gram-positive coccus in clusters. The isolate grows right up to a novobiocin disk with no surrounding zone of inhibition. Which organism is this?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Enterococcus faecalis

choices.label: B
choices.text: Staphylococcus aureus

choices.label: C
choices.text: Staphylococcus epidermidis

choices.label: D
choices.text: Staphylococcus saprophyticus

choices.label: E
choices.text: Streptococcus agalactiae

explanation.summary: Novobiocin resistance separates S. saprophyticus from S. epidermidis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Among the coagulase-negative staphylococci, novobiocin is the deciding test: S. saprophyticus is novobiocin resistant while S. epidermidis is novobiocin sensitive. Growth right up to the disk with no clear ring means the organism is resistant.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Enterococcus faecalis is also catalase negative and grows in chains rather than clusters.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Staphylococcus aureus is coagulase positive, which the stem has excluded.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Staphylococcus epidermidis is novobiocin sensitive and would show a zone of inhibition.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Streptococcus agalactiae is a catalase-negative coccus in chains, not a staphylococcus in clusters.

questions.stem: An alpha-hemolytic, catalase-negative gram-positive coccus is plated on blood agar with an optochin disk, and a clear ring of no growth surrounds the disk. Which organism is identified?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Enterococcus faecalis

choices.label: B
choices.text: Staphylococcus aureus

choices.label: C
choices.text: Streptococcus mitis

choices.label: D
choices.text: Streptococcus mutans

choices.label: E
choices.text: Streptococcus pneumoniae

explanation.summary: Optochin sensitivity identifies S. pneumoniae among the alpha-hemolytic streptococci.
explanation.whyCorrect: Alpha-hemolytic streptococci are sorted by optochin sensitivity and bile solubility. S. pneumoniae is optochin sensitive, while the viridans streptococci are optochin resistant. An empty ring around the disk means the organism is susceptible.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Enterococcus faecalis shows gamma hemolysis rather than the alpha pattern described.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Staphylococcus aureus is catalase positive, which the stem has excluded.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Streptococcus mitis is likewise a viridans organism and is optochin resistant.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Streptococcus mutans is a viridans streptococcus and is optochin resistant, growing up to the disk.

questions.stem: Two beta-hemolytic, catalase-negative streptococci are tested with bacitracin disks. Isolate 1 shows a wide zone of inhibition around the disk, and isolate 2 grows up to the disk. Which identification fits isolate 1?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Enterococcus faecium

choices.label: B
choices.text: Streptococcus agalactiae, Group B

choices.label: C
choices.text: Streptococcus mutans

choices.label: D
choices.text: Streptococcus pneumoniae

choices.label: E
choices.text: Streptococcus pyogenes, Group A

explanation.summary: Bacitracin sensitivity identifies Group A Streptococcus pyogenes.
explanation.whyCorrect: The beta-hemolytic streptococci are separated by bacitracin sensitivity: S. pyogenes, Group A, is bacitracin sensitive, while S. agalactiae, Group B, is bacitracin resistant. A wide zone of inhibition therefore identifies isolate 1 as S. pyogenes.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Enterococcus faecium is sorted from the gamma-hemolytic branch of the algorithm.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Streptococcus agalactiae is bacitracin resistant and matches isolate 2, which grew up to the disk.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Streptococcus mutans belongs to the alpha-hemolytic viridans group.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Streptococcus pneumoniae is alpha hemolytic, not beta hemolytic as described.

questions.stem: Two alpha-hemolytic isolates are each mixed with a bile salt solution. Tube 1 becomes clear, and tube 2 remains cloudy. Which conclusion is best supported?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Tube 1 holds a viridans streptococcus, which is lysed by bile

choices.label: B
choices.text: Tube 1 holds Enterococcus faecalis, which is lysed by bile

choices.label: C
choices.text: Tube 1 holds Streptococcus pneumoniae, which is lysed by bile

choices.label: D
choices.text: Tube 2 holds Staphylococcus aureus, which resists bile

choices.label: E
choices.text: Tube 2 holds Streptococcus pneumoniae, which resists bile

explanation.summary: Bile solubility, seen as clearing of the media, identifies Streptococcus pneumoniae.
explanation.whyCorrect: Some bacteria resist lysis by bile salts and others do not. S. pneumoniae is lysed in bile salts, so the media start to clear, which is reported as bile soluble. Organisms that are not lysed leave the media cloudy.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Viridans streptococci resist being dissolved by bile salts, so they leave the media cloudy.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Enterococcus spp. also resist bile lysis and would not clear the tube.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Staphylococcus aureus is a catalase-positive coccus in clusters and is not an alpha-hemolytic isolate.
whyWrongByChoice.E: S. pneumoniae is bile soluble, so it belongs to the tube that cleared, not the cloudy one.

questions.stem: A gram-positive bacillus recovered from a deep wound grows in the anaerobic incubator but fails to grow in the incubator supplied with oxygen. Which genus is most consistent with this result?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Bacillus

choices.label: B
choices.text: Clostridium

choices.label: C
choices.text: Corynebacterium

choices.label: D
choices.text: Listeria

choices.label: E
choices.text: Nocardia

explanation.summary: Among gram-positive rods, Clostridium spp. are the obligate anaerobes.
explanation.whyCorrect: Oxygen requirement is one of the first branch points for gram-positive bacilli. Bacillus spp. are aerobes, while Clostridium spp. are obligate anaerobes that grow only when oxygen is absent, which matches this isolate.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Bacillus spp. are aerobes and would have grown in the oxygenated incubator.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Corynebacterium is likewise grouped with the aerobic gram-positive rods.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Listeria sits on the aerobic branch of the gram-positive bacilli.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Nocardia is an aerobe and forms branching filaments rather than simple rods.

questions.stem: A gram-positive organism forms branching filaments on Gram stain. It grows in an oxygenated incubator, and an acid-fast stain shows weak staining. Which identification fits best?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Actinomyces, an aerobe that is weakly acid fast

choices.label: B
choices.text: Actinomyces, an anaerobe that is not acid fast

choices.label: C
choices.text: Clostridium, an anaerobe that is not acid fast

choices.label: D
choices.text: Corynebacterium, an aerobe that is weakly acid fast

choices.label: E
choices.text: Nocardia, an aerobe that is weakly acid fast

explanation.summary: Aerobic, weakly acid-fast branching filaments are Nocardia; anaerobic, non-acid-fast ones are Actinomyces.
explanation.whyCorrect: Branching filaments form their own limb of the gram-positive algorithm, split by oxygen requirement. Nocardia is the aerobic branching organism and is weakly acid fast, while Actinomyces is the anaerobic one and is not acid fast.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Actinomyces is anaerobic and not acid fast, so this pairing misstates the organism.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Actinomyces is correctly described here as an anaerobe that is not acid fast, which does not match this aerobic, weakly acid-fast isolate.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Clostridium organisms are rods rather than branching filaments, and they grow only anaerobically.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Corynebacterium organisms are club-shaped rods and are not described as acid fast.

questions.stem: Cerebrospinal fluid from a patient with meningitis grows gram-negative diplococci on Thayer-Martin agar. The isolate produces acid from maltose. Which organism is identified?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Bordetella pertussis

choices.label: B
choices.text: Haemophilus influenzae

choices.label: C
choices.text: Moraxella spp.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Neisseria gonorrhoeae

choices.label: E
choices.text: Neisseria meningitidis

explanation.summary: Maltose acid detection separates N. meningitidis from N. gonorrhoeae.
explanation.whyCorrect: In the gram-negative algorithm, aerobic diplococci are sorted by maltose acid detection. A positive result identifies Neisseria meningitidis, while a negative result points to N. gonorrhoeae or Moraxella.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Bordetella pertussis also belongs to the coccobacilli rather than the diplococci.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Haemophilus influenzae is a gram-negative coccobacillus, not a diplococcus.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Moraxella is grouped with N. gonorrhoeae as maltose negative.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Neisseria gonorrhoeae falls on the maltose-negative branch of the algorithm.

questions.stem: A curved, oxidase-positive gram-negative rod is recovered from a gastric biopsy. The isolate hydrolyzes urea. Which organism is identified?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Campylobacter jejuni

choices.label: B
choices.text: Helicobacter pylori

choices.label: C
choices.text: Pseudomonas aeruginosa

choices.label: D
choices.text: Salmonella enterica

choices.label: E
choices.text: Vibrio cholerae

explanation.summary: Among the oxidase-positive curved rods, urease production identifies Helicobacter pylori.
explanation.whyCorrect: Curved gram-negative rods that are oxidase positive are separated by three features: growth at 42 degrees Celsius, growth in alkaline media, and urease production. Urease production is the branch that identifies Helicobacter pylori.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Campylobacter jejuni is identified by its growth at 42 degrees Celsius rather than by urease.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Pseudomonas aeruginosa is a straight bacillus sorted by lactose fermentation and oxidase status.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Salmonella enterica is a straight bacillus identified by H2S production on TSI agar.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Vibrio cholerae is identified by its growth in alkaline media.

questions.stem: A gram-negative bacillus from a burn wound does not ferment lactose on MacConkey agar. A sample of the colony placed on oxidase reagent turns dark purple within seconds. Which organism is most likely?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Escherichia coli

choices.label: B
choices.text: Klebsiella pneumoniae

choices.label: C
choices.text: Pseudomonas spp.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Salmonella spp.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Shigella spp.

explanation.summary: A non-lactose-fermenting, oxidase-positive gram-negative bacillus is Pseudomonas.
explanation.whyCorrect: The oxidase test detects cytochrome c oxidase and is used to separate Pseudomonas spp. from other gram-negative bacilli. Pseudomonas spp. are oxidase positive, turning the reagent blue or dark purple, while most Enterobacteriaceae are oxidase negative.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Escherichia coli is oxidase negative and ferments lactose rapidly.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Klebsiella pneumoniae is a lactose fermenter and is oxidase negative.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Salmonella spp. are also oxidase negative and are distinguished by producing H2S.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Shigella spp. are oxidase negative and are sorted further by H2S production.

questions.stem: An isolate is inoculated into urea broth containing phenol red. After incubation, the broth has turned pink. Which change in the medium produced this color?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Acid from sugar fermentation lowered the pH

choices.label: B
choices.text: Ammonia from urea raised the pH

choices.label: C
choices.text: Oxidized cytochrome c darkened the indicator

choices.label: D
choices.text: Oxygen from peroxide breakdown aerated the broth

choices.label: E
choices.text: Sulfide precipitated with iron in the broth

explanation.summary: A pink urea broth means urease generated alkaline ammonia.
explanation.whyCorrect: Urease hydrolyzes urea into ammonia and carbon dioxide. Ammonia is basic, so the medium becomes alkaline and phenol red turns pink, which is a positive urease result.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Acid production lowers the pH and is what turns TSI agar yellow, the opposite of this reaction.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Oxidase activity is read on filter paper with oxidase reagent, which turns blue or dark purple.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Breakdown of hydrogen peroxide to oxygen is the catalase reaction, read as bubbling.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Sulfide reacting with iron forms the black precipitate of a positive H2S result on TSI agar.

questions.stem: A catalase-negative, gram-positive coccus growing in chains causes no hemolysis on blood agar and grows in broth containing 6.5% sodium chloride. Which organism is most consistent with this result?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Enterococcus faecalis

choices.label: B
choices.text: Streptococcus agalactiae

choices.label: C
choices.text: Streptococcus bovis

choices.label: D
choices.text: Streptococcus pneumoniae

choices.label: E
choices.text: Streptococcus pyogenes

explanation.summary: Growth in 6.5% NaCl separates Enterococcus from the nonenterococcal gamma-hemolytic streptococci.
explanation.whyCorrect: Catalase-negative cocci in chains with no hemolysis fall on the gamma branch of the gram-positive algorithm, where growth in 6.5% sodium chloride and PYR status are the deciding tests. Growth in the high-salt broth identifies Enterococcus, such as E. faecalis.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Streptococcus agalactiae is also beta hemolytic rather than non-hemolytic.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Streptococcus bovis is the nonenterococcal organism on this branch and does not grow in 6.5% sodium chloride.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Streptococcus pneumoniae is alpha hemolytic and grows in pairs with pointed ends.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Streptococcus pyogenes is beta hemolytic and would clear the blood agar.

questions.stem: A 27-year-old man has fever, vomiting, abdominal cramps, and diarrhea two days after a potluck at which he ate chicken that was pink in the center. Stool culture grows a gram-negative bacillus that does not ferment lactose, is oxidase negative, and produces H2S on triple sugar iron agar. Which organism is the most likely cause?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Escherichia coli

choices.label: B
choices.text: Pseudomonas spp.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Salmonella spp.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Shigella spp.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Vibrio cholerae

explanation.summary: A non-lactose-fermenting, oxidase-negative, H2S-positive gram-negative bacillus from stool is Salmonella.
explanation.whyCorrect: The gram-negative algorithm sorts bacilli first by lactose fermentation, then by oxidase status, then by H2S production on TSI agar. A non-fermenting, oxidase-negative, H2S-positive isolate lands on the Salmonella branch, which fits gastroenteritis after undercooked chicken.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Escherichia coli ferments lactose rapidly, so it would not be a non-fermenter.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Pseudomonas spp. are oxidase positive, which the stem has excluded.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Shigella spp. sit on the same branch but are H2S negative on TSI agar.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Vibrio cholerae is a curved, oxidase-positive rod identified by growth in alkaline media.
